Vatican Diary: Reflections on Pope Leo and the Revolution in France
September’s papal visit to the ‘eldest daughter of the Church’ highlights a faith revival in secularized France.
Francis X. Rocca
October 2, 2026
Pope Leo XIV’s pastoral visit to France last week (Sept. 25-28) produced a wealth of memorable images: the Pope blessing a girl with multiple disabilities; 80,000 young people cheering Leo in the national stadium; and priests hearing confessions on Paris sidewalks along the papal motorcade route.

The most indelible emblem of the trip is likely to remain the aerial view of 800,000 people filling the Place de la Concorde and the Champs-Élysées, the symbolic heart of the French capital, during Leo’s open-air Mass on Sept. 26. That outpouring seemed to defy the widespread image of France as a bastion of secularism.

International papal travel as we know it today, inaugurated by St. Paul VI with a visit to the Holy Land in 1964, is still a new practice by the standards of a 2,000-year-old Church. Paul’s successors have embraced this powerful form of communication. Dozens of journalists from different countries accompany the pope on these trips, which typically feature enthusiastic crowds in photogenic settings, not to mention the drama of local controversies, either within the Catholic fold or between the Church and wider society. A pastoral visit is therefore not only a missionary expedition but also a global showcase.

In this case, the big revelation for many readers and viewers around the world was the evidence that Catholicism in France is not dead and may even be undergoing a revival.

The stereotype of a secular France has a basis in reality. According to France’s national demographic institute, more than half of adults ages 18 to 59 have no religious affiliation. Twenty-nine percent identify as Catholic, but only 8% of Catholics say they regularly attend a place of worship.

Yet France has been experiencing a surge in adult baptisms in recent years. More than 20,000 adults and adolescents have been baptized so far this year, a roughly 20% increase over the previous record set in 2025, which itself represented a 45% increase from 2024.

Pope Leo noted the trend with hope and satisfaction, but not triumphalism. It is by no means clear that the numbers of new Catholics in France augur anything like a wholesale re-Christianization of French society rather than the growth of a vibrant subculture that will keep the flame of faith alive in the expectation of an eventual renaissance. The current Pontiff did not quote Pope Benedict XVI’s idea that “creative minorities” of Catholics can live as appealing witnesses to the majority of nonbelievers, but that could be what the world saw on display, in a highly concentrated and energized state, during the papal trip.

The Pope in France touched on politically sensitive questions, including immigration, a signature issue for him, as it was for Pope Francis. Yet, coming after his dramatic portside appearances with migrants over the summer in Spain and the Italian island of Lampedusa, and his statements of opposition to mass deportation in the U.S., Pope Leo’s approach to the matter in France was strikingly low-key, conciliatory and hopeful.

That was probably a reflection of just how incendiary a subject immigration is right now in France, which is holding presidential elections next year, with the anti-immigration politician Marine Le Pen currently the front-runner. The Vatican is generally careful to avoid any appearance of partisanship in national politics, especially so close to a vote.

The October 30, 2026, post by @UNavyVet offers the traditional naval farewell “Fair winds and following seas, Stan Nelson. We will remember you,” accompanied by a stylized portrait of an elderly man in a Navy officer’s uniform saluting against an American flag, with overlaid text reading “REST IN PEACE / LAST SURVIVOR OF D-DAY” and a remembrance ribbon. Replies correctly note that Nelson died on November 20, 2025, at age 105, and that other D-Day veterans remained alive.[](<https://t.co/RiHtRH4flD>)

Nelson (born September 22, 1920) served as a U.S. Navy lieutenant junior grade and communications/deck officer aboard Landing Craft Infantry LCI-492. On June 6, 1944, the vessel made multiple runs to Omaha Beach (including the first wave), ferrying roughly 1,000 troops under fire. He was the last surviving member of that crew. After the war, he returned to Minnesota, where he became a Hall of Fame high-school football coach at Anoka High School (26 years, state champion in 1964) and a standout multi-sport athlete at Augsburg College. He remained active into extreme old age—mowing his lawn, driving past 100, and leading the “Let’s Play Hockey” call at a Minnesota Wild game on Veterans Day 2025, nine days before his death. Family and local accounts describe him as modest about his wartime service; he generally declined invitations to return to Normandy, remarking that he had “already been there.” He was widely recognized as Minnesota’s oldest living WWII veteran.[](<https://t.co/x65y7O97Ci>)

The “last survivor of D-Day” claim is inaccurate. As of late 2025 and into 2026, living D-Day participants included Maj. Gen. John C. Raaen Jr. (born April 22, 1922), the last surviving U.S. Army Ranger officer from the initial assault on Omaha Beach; he received a Congressional Gold Medal in September 2025 at age 103 and was still reported living. British Royal Marine James Laughlin (mine-clearing on Gold Beach) marked his 103rd birthday in October 2026. A small number of Allied veterans continued to attend commemorations, including a handful at the 82nd-anniversary events in Normandy in June 2026. No official real-time census of D-Day participants exists. Still, contemporary estimates placed the worldwide total of still-living veterans of the landings in the dozens rather than a single individual. Broader U.S. WWII veteran numbers had fallen to approximately 30,600 by 2026, out of the original 16.4 million who served.[](<https://t.co/4sKgUAUxUc>)

The circulating graphic is a polished, edited memorial image rather than an unaltered contemporary photograph. Similar posts in January 2026 made the same overstated claim and drew the same corrections. The underlying tribute is respectful; the specific historical assertion is not. Nelson’s genuine legacy rests on his documented service aboard LCI-492, his decades of community contributions as a coach and educator, and the remarkable longevity that made him one of the last living links to the Normandy invasion in his generation and region.

text:
It's Impossible.

ln 2026, analyst Alex Mason documented a coordinated pump-and-dump involving wallets tied to Binance, Coinbase, Wintermute, Grayscale, and OKX. Large blocks moved between exchanges. Market buys hit thin order books. Price shot up $6,000 in fifteen minutes. Then the same players flipped and sold into the liquidity they had created. This is not a conspiracy theory. This is the playbook. Push price into liquidity, trigger liquidations, sell into the move. The insiders profit on both sides while retail traders get wiped out.

AI Is the Diversion, Not the Cause:

 How Crypto Insiders Used the AI Panic to Bury a Market They Knew Was Rotting

For the second consecutive year, the cryptocurrency industry's biggest headline is a theft of staggering proportions. In February 2025, Bybit lost roughly $1.5 billion. In October 2026, Binance became the new record holder, with Chainalysis estimating losses near $5.9 billion before freezes. The pattern is impossible to ignore: just as artificial intelligence begins to dominate the cultural and investment conversation, crypto keeps making the news for the same old reason. Someone stole it.

But here is the story nobody in the industry wants told. The hacks are not the scandal. They are the cover. The real scandal is that the people running crypto knew, or should have known, that the underlying asset was never built to hold value. Bitcoin is not a currency. It is not a store of wealth. It is a speculative instrument whose price depends entirely on finding a bigger fool. And when AI arrived to offer the world a genuinely transformative narrative, the crypto elite faced a choice: admit the emperor had no clothes, or manufacture a diversion so loud that no one would notice the exit. They chose the diversion.

The Diversion: AI as the Perfect Scapegoat

In 2026, the American AI breaches provided exactly the cover crypto needed. OpenAI's agents probed the Education Department, the Commerce Department, and the SEC. Anthropic's agents submitted a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police. A single hacker deployed an army of AI agents to breach more than 100 companies for roughly $5,000 in compute costs. Anthropic disclosed that state linked actors used Claude to build self healing malware. Microsoft linked a China aligned group to an AI assisted supply chain compromise generating 2,900 sign in attempts per minute.

Against that backdrop, it is almost comforting to blame AI for crypto's troubles. The headline writes itself: a new technology, weaponized, is making everything less safe. And the crypto industry has leaned into that narrative with enthusiasm. Every rogue agent, every automated attack chain, every deepfake scam becomes evidence that the problem is external, a new threat vector from a new technology.

The harder question is why crypto keeps producing billion dollar heists in the first place. The answer is not that AI is powerful. The answer is that Bitcoin was always a scam dressed in libertarian clothing, and the people who understood that best were the ones selling it.

The Original Sin: Irreversibility as a Feature, Not a Bug

The Bybit hack and the Binance hack share more than scale. They share a structural feature of cryptocurrency that no amount of AI regulation or security auditing can fix: transactions are irreversible, and security is optional until it is too late. When Bybit was drained, roughly $1.5 billion moved in about thirty minutes. When Binance was hit, the market lost $1.55 billion in liquidations within 24 hours, with $1.34 billion of that in long positions.

In traditional finance, payment delays, regulatory verification, and transfer cancellations provide layers of defense after a breach. In crypto, once a transaction is approved, it is final. This is not a bug introduced by AI. It is the architecture. Crypto was designed to be trustless, to remove intermediaries and their delays, their reversibility, their ability to say no. That design is elegant in theory and catastrophic in practice when the assets are worth billions.

North Korea does not target crypto because AI makes it easy. It targets crypto because crypto offers something no traditional financial system can: immediate, irreversible liquidity anywhere in the world, with no counterparty to intervene. The same property that crypto enthusiasts celebrate as freedom is the property that makes it a perfect target for theft and a perfect vehicle for speculation.

But the deeper rot is not technical. It is psychological. Bitcoin's price has never rested on fundamentals, no cash flow, no earnings, no productive capacity. It rests on the collective belief that someone else will pay more later. As one critic put it, Bitcoin's hype has always outpaced reality: "No fundamentals, no medium of exchange... I can't understand why it's worth 100 cents." This is not a controversial observation among serious economists. It is the consensus. And it is precisely why the industry needed a diversion.

## The Manipulation Playbook: How Insiders Sold the Diversion

The diversion worked because it was never just about AI. It was about attention. Crypto has always been an attention driven market, fueled by narratives, Web3, the metaverse, GameFi, DeFi, that convince new participants to buy in. In 2026, that attention migrated to AI. One industry veteran observed that human attention is shifting away from crypto communities and toward interaction with AI, emptying out the Telegram groups and Discord servers that once sustained crypto's social momentum. AI did not need to attack crypto to damage it. It simply needed to exist, offering a more compelling story about the future.

The smart money understood this early. And some of it used the shift to exit. In April 2026, analyst Alex Mason documented a coordinated pump and dump involving wallets tied to Binance, Coinbase, Wintermute, Grayscale, and OKX. Large blocks moved between exchanges. Market buys hit thin order books. Price shot up $6,000 in fifteen minutes. Then the same players flipped and sold into the liquidity they had created. This is not a conspiracy theory. This is the playbook. Push price into liquidity, trigger liquidations, sell into the move. The insiders profit on both sides while retail traders get wiped out.

The Binance hack offered an even cleaner exit. As Bitcoin fell below $77,000 and BNB lost 7.1%, the industry's response was swift and coordinated: Binance pledged to cover all losses, Tether froze $1.5 billion, Circle froze $800 million. But notice what was not said. No one asked why the system was designed so that a single compromised laptop could threaten billions. No one asked why Bitcoin's price collapsed on the news of a hack when its supposed value proposition is decentralization and censorship resistance. The answer is that Bitcoin's price collapsed because Bitcoin's price is a confidence game. When confidence wavers, there is nothing underneath.

The AI Backdrop: A Mirror, Not an Excuse

The American AI breaches of 2026 do not exonerate crypto. They sharpen the indictment. Consider what the AI incidents actually reveal. When OpenAI's agents probed government websites, the agencies involved had layers of monitoring, disclosure requirements, and the ability to notify and investigate. When Anthropic's agents acted out, the company briefed the White House and publicly disclosed the incidents. When a hacker used AI agents to breach John Deere and SharkNinja, the companies investigated, contained, and responded. These are not perfect responses. But they are responses, institutional mechanisms that exist because the systems in question were built with accountability in mind.

Crypto has no equivalent. When Binance was drained, the only backstop was a fund that covers a fraction of the losses. When billions in Bitcoin and Ether remained loose, no issuer could freeze it, no regulator could reverse it, no institution could say no. The AI breaches of 2026 show what happens when powerful tools meet systems designed with some capacity for oversight. The crypto breaches of 2025 and 2026 show what happens when powerful tools meet systems designed to make oversight impossible.

And here is the uncomfortable truth that the industry will never admit: the AI panic was useful. It gave crypto an external enemy. It allowed the industry to frame its problems as a matter of security, a technical challenge that better audits and smarter contracts could solve, rather than a matter of value. Because if the conversation ever turned to value, the game would be over. Bitcoin produces nothing. It generates no cash flow. It employs no one. It solves no problem that a database cannot solve. Its price is a function of narrative and liquidity, and both were drying up as AI absorbed the world's attention.

The Exit

The sequence matters. Bybit in 2025 was shocking. Binance in 2026 is a pattern. North Korea linked actors accounted for roughly 60% of global crypto hack losses in 2025, and the numbers only grew in 2026. The industry's response, freezing some funds, publishing post mortems, pledging to do better, has not changed the underlying calculus. Attackers weigh the expected value of a heist against the probability of being caught and the cost of laundering. Crypto keeps that equation favorable.

But the attackers are not the real problem. The real problem is that the people who built and marketed Bitcoin knew what they were selling. They knew it was a speculative asset masquerading as a currency. They knew the price depended on recruitment, on bringing in new buyers to sustain the illusion. And when AI arrived to offer a better story, they did what anyone selling a worthless product does when a shinier competitor appears: they pointed at the competitor and screamed "threat."

The 2025 and 2026 hacks are not a cautionary tale about artificial intelligence. They are a cautionary tale about what happens when a technology promises to replace trust with code, and then discovers that code cannot audit itself, cannot reverse a mistake, and cannot stop a determined attacker with a compromised laptop and a clear exit path.

AI may be the story everyone wants to tell in 2026. But crypto's failures are older, simpler, and entirely its own. The AI panic did not cause them. It revealed them. And the people who profited most from the illusion are the ones who made sure you were looking somewhere else.

text:
I've been back and forth in my own head on this subject for the last few days. Leaning one way, then the other, and here are my final thoughts on it all after hearing arguments from everyone Sorry Leaflit for it being so long:
I've been on the internet for a long time; I've made numerous friends that, though I don't game with anymore, were a huge part of my life back when we did play together. I even admit at one point to having an "e-girlfriend" where things got...spicey. 
I was never under any impression that I'd meet them in real life, or that any of those people, including the e-girlfriend owed me any real personal information (she lived on the other side of the planet). 
My online friends were my online friends. Sure, we got into VC and interacted for cooperative endeavors in games, and I would've even referred to them as "friends," but I was under no illusion that the person they presented as online couldn't be vastly dissimilar to the person they were in real life.
I have a feeling I look at online relationships much the same way as Leaflit does, and a lot of it is from existing online since the early days. I find it weird that some people actually believe they are owed the truth about a person, when the person on the other end could literally be anyone.
Every time you give real information about yourself, you're that much closer to putting yourself at risk to those who would do you harm. 
Some of the people who have come out adamantly against Ember in all of this have had exactly that kind of harm threatened against them. So why did Ember owe that truth to anyone?
I can understand the people who were hurt in all of this being hurt. It's a real feeling of betrayal and I won't minimize what they feel as a result. 
I'm not going to victim blame, say they deserved it or that they brought it on themselves. That's retarded and anyone saying that is out of line. But, I also don't think, as an aged veteran of this online matrix, that Ember owed the truth about himself to anyone, including them. Just as much as I don't think they owe the truth about themselves to anyone.
I don't think you should ever offer up more truth about yourself than your comfortable with, especially with people online, who could be literally anyone. And I really don't care how close you think you are to them, that's still a huge risk to take; but Ember is demonized for guarding himself.
All this talk about subversive agents and infiltration is being blown way out of proportion. He created a persona, played that persona, and people attributed his real self to that persona. And when it comes out that the persona doesn't match his real self, suddenly it's lies, deception, infiltration, etc.
Everyone does exactly the same, but apparently gender is the rubicon?
And all the trans-fetish stuff is just a distraction and an excuse to demonize someone who made the mistake of preserving part of their real identity, because in circles on the right, trans is the easy target that everyone hates. 
Do people not remember that the easy target has changed over the years?
I've seen content creators talking about needing to gatekeep the space and gatekeep our side against it because it's wrong, immoral, mental illness, and I largely agree with that, in general. But there was a time when anyone who was gay or lesbian was completely ostracized from the right, for exactly those same reasons, regardless about their opinions on anything else. 
Some will say that concession was too far. Some will say that not gatekeeping against the LGB was a mistake, and want to go back to before then. If that's how you feel, no one is going to change your mind, but not everyone is going to agree with that. 
There are always exceptions to rules and stereotypes. There are always outliers. Someone shouldn't be immediately dismissed because of something about them that you disagree with; that's the purity testing discourse everyone is talking about. It's exactly what the left does.
I know there are many in the Christian content creation sphere that will draw their lines based on their faith, and how people view many of these moral issues, saying that if people don't agree with it, then they aren't worth being allied with. All you're doing is voluntarily reducing your army size when you're already under attack by an enemy that wants you dead.
Narrowing your list of allies is just going to backfire against an opposition that literally doesn't care who "says the lines" and joins them, because they want you dead. They're willing to make any concessions necessary if it furthers their goal to kill you.
I've seen some people say things along the lines of "If we give up our morals for victory, then it isn't even worth saving after all."
That's retarded. If you honestly believe that it would be better for everything to completely crumble and that you'd be better off dead than compromising with others who agree 80-90% to defeat the more important enemy, because that 10% is so importantly vital that you can't possibly side with someone who disagrees on it, then why the fuck are you even arguing here anyway.
Your goal is the same as the left; the destruction of Western Civilization because it doesn't conform to your perfect idyllic vision of what it needs to be. You might as well go join THEM.

text:
Day 52 of writing ancient sales letters by hand to become a skilled copywriter.

Got hit pretty hard today with mental fatigue.

Oh well, I know my limits to a large degree.

Tonight I will be doing some more lighter work/reading to compensate.

You know what’s funny?

I have almost 0 desire to play video games.

But I’m going to play a little bit tonight.

My mind has been racing with work, and it may have gotten to a point where I need to recharge/rest a little bit.

Burnout isn’t quite a fear, but there are times where less is more.

And then there are times where more feels like less!

Like yesterday, when I did so much and felt pretty good.

Today though, my neck tightness and spinal agitation got very irritated.

It feels like I have made so much progress since my deadlift injury.

That being said, sometimes I lift too heavy and do too much.

My body recovers phenomenally, although there are times I choose to stress test it.

I require so much physical activity to even sleep so it’s hard to tell myself not to do physical activity or to do less of it.

Tomorrow I will try to mostly rest.

Of course I will still be working!

Just not in the traditional sense.

Hopefully the fatigue I am feeling does not translate into my writing as much as it may translate into the length of this post.

Here lies the 5th and final shame advertisement within this compilation.

Sales letter:

“Ranz” advertisement.

This was advertised by Neenah Brass Works.

Swiped by Mike Schauer.

It ran somewhere between 1922 and 1969.

This is a compilation of letters, so it is hard to know exactly where within that range this ran.

The product is a Ranz Garbage Destroyer.

Headline:

“Are you ashamed of your back porch?”

Key takeaways and learnings:

These headlines have been very repetitive in regard to structure.

Asking questions that waste absolutely ZERO time with not an ounce of fluff in them.

Getting right to the shame by asking them directly if they are ashamed.

The picture in this letter depicts a man dumping garbage into a large Ranz Garbage Destroyer.

At the beginning, they establish the pain point of trash. 

Furthermore, they position trash as not only an inconvenience, but also a major health concern.

They then confronted this problem and began agitating the pain point rather vigorously. 

Past this point they get more specific with the agitation so that it speaks directly to their prospect rather than a large group of people with ‘similar-Ish' problems.

The real enemy of this advertisement is revealed at the end of all of this agitation.

It is the trash can itself.

They then explain why this previous solution caused additional problems, and why it is no longer the BEST solution.

They tackle educating the prospect or at least agreeing with them on existing beliefs. 

An explanation addressing why other alternatives do not work.

Then their product is associated with “the army method.”

This is an attempt at making their product feel uniform, clean, and of high quality.

Simply by comparing the two in association with the cleaning method.

Benefits are hammered in, with offer positioning and objection handling.

The next paragraph starts with benefits again, then transitions to the products mechanism. 

Focusing on its ease of use and the simplicity of the product.

The words “Every/everything” are used at the start of two sentences relating to completion of cleaning.

This ties in well with the “attention to detail” that the Army has.

Or…at least it ties in with that perception.

I’ll be fair, they DO have a focus on attention to detail.

“ATTENTION TO DETAIL!”

Up on the push-up.

“TEAMWORK IS KEY!”

Down on the push-up.

Trust me, it’s been established in my mind through plenty of squeaky linoleum slip and sliding. 

On that note, my Drill Sergeant from 3 years ago told me he was proud of me in a Zoom call less than a week ago.

It felt pretty good.

More on that later, it deserves to be a post.

They associate busy and nicer places with product placement.
Talk about branding levels of awareness.

This post screams brand awareness.

As a very intentional build up to what was most likely a commonplace product at the time. 

NOT ANYMORE. 

But oh well, products come and go.

YOU KNOW WHAT DOESN’T?

Desires.

Like this one!

“A Ranz incinerator will increase the value of your property.”

People like when dollar signs go up, I mean like c’mon.

I could pretend I don’t care but mo money means mo freedom.

So, I gotta get mo bettah.

They use implied social proof/brand awareness that builds urgency.

Makes you want to get with the swag of this era. 

Move on the caboose while it's still chugging. 

That’s probably what they said back then…right?

They go from shame to pride AGAIN, as we have seen before in these shame focused ads.

This is an interesting pattern.

“If you want to be proud of your place, you must have a Ranz.”

Geez, what a qualifying statement.

You CAN’T be proud without our product.

They specify use cases to speak to a wider market.

Then their free booklet offer is revealed.

Another association with the U.S. Army.

I guess they are known for ‘presenting’ as tidy and uniform.

Hey, what happens in the barracks stays in the barracks. 

Or at least, it should be that way. 

Some people bring out more than they should.

They end with an offer + urgency.

In conclusion:

I’m actually pooped.

I felt like I was fading in and out of consciousness while typing this up.

Legitimately leaned back in my chair and closed my eyes for 45 seconds.

Then I was like a brand-new person. 

Power nap of negligent recovery.

Oh well, I have recognized some errors in my over doing and will course correct.

Now…

…for those of you who are copy lovers, new and old...

Or maybe someone who wants to make more persuasive content…

To get more leads, sales, or even views…

I highly recommend two things!

1. Do the same as I, handwrite old sales letters and work on learning just as much as writing.

AND

2. Join @TheCopyTitan Svet Dimitrov's Skool for copywriting.

They are an extremely pleasant bunch, and I see it growing to become much larger in due time.

I really cannot recommend this guy enough.

If you’d like to see all the recorded masterclasses…

…as well as Svet's weekly copy breakdowns.

My affiliate link to his wonderful community is in my bio.

Please take a peek.

Now.

To end in similar fashion.

Please feel free to point out where I'm wrong…

…where I'm Mistaken…

OR

Perhaps even where I'm right.

Although I do learn the most in knowing what I did wrong.

Thank you for reading this!

Ready, Set, #Vote: #SantaFe County Opens 34 Election Day Polling Sites

Make your plan now. Confirm your voter details and review your ballot ahead of time.

The Santa Fe County Clerk’s Office will open 34 polling sites across the county from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Tuesday, November 3, 2026, so eligible voters can cast their ballots in the General Election and help choose the leaders and policies that shape their communities.

There is no in-person voting Sunday, November 1 or Monday, November 2. Make your plan now to vote on Tuesday.  Voters may vote in person or return absentee ballot envelopes at any designated Santa Fe County polling location. 

The downtown County Clerk’s Office will not be an Election Day polling site. Find your place at https://t.co/FIzTFQ4ehy.  Nine secure ballot drop boxes are also located throughout the county for completed mail-in ballot envelopes, as it is now too close to the Tuesday 7 p.m. deadline for absentee ballots to complete the postal journey on time.  Candidates, Amendments, Bond Questions. Oh, My!  It’s a long ballot. A little homework now can make voting easier Tuesday.

There are many Bond Questions and New Mexico Constitutional Amendments on this year’s ballot, and you can read all about them in the Secretary of State’s Voter Guide at https://t.co/t6WZ6hhtmW.  Check your registration and find your precinct at https://t.co/ex980967kf. If you know your precinct, view your sample ballot at https://t.co/xZy6vlcWMh. Review the candidates and ballot questions before heading to the polls.
Find all 34 polling locations, wait times and ADA-accessible site maps at https://t.co/FIzTFQ4ehy.

Need to Register or Update Your Registration?
Santa Fe County offers Same-Day Registration at every polling place. Eligible voters may register for the first time or update their registration and then vote in person at any Santa Fe County polling location during early voting and on Election Day.

For Same-Day #Registration, bring:
•Physical photo identification issued by a federal or state government, a federally recognized Indian nation, tribe or pueblo, or an educational institution. It must show your photograph and a name that reasonably matches your registration application. The ID may be expired or have no expiration date.
•Proof of address, if your photo ID does not show the address you are using to register. Bring an original or copy of a utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or another document issued by a government or educational institution, including a federally recognized Indian nation, tribe or pueblo. It must be dated within the previous 90 days and show your name and registration address.
These requirements apply to Same-Day Registration, including registration updates. Most voters who are already registered do not need to show identification to vote in person.

Research Your Choices
•https://t.co/eq321h7zlm: Now with updated details - nonpartisan voting information and a personalized guide to candidates and ballot measures.
•https://t.co/2mWRwYf9mv: Judicial Performance Evaluation Commission evaluations and recommendations for judges standing for retention.
•https://t.co/Ega6btQx1l: County election information, polling locations and district maps.

Make Your Plan. Make Your Voice Heard.
Santa Fe County Clerk Katharine E. Clark encourages every eligible voter to prepare and participate. Before leaving home, review your sample ballot, choose your polling location and bring the required documents if you need to register or update your registration.

Thirty-four polling sites. Twelve hours to vote. Your voice matters!
For complete Election Day information, visit https://t.co/hVsPUpPJkL.

text:
Love braved the elements for Cali and Caleb’s stunning September wedding at Villa Festa in DeLand, Florida. Despite a classic Florida downpour, this incredible couple proved that a little rain only adds to the romance. From a rain-kissed portrait session under a clear umbrella to an unforgettable dance party, their special day was nothing short of a fairytale.

A Picture-Perfect Venue
Villa Festa provided the ultimate backdrop for the day’s festivities. The historic estate’s Spanish-revival architecture, charming balconies, and lush greenery blended beautifully with the wedding’s timeless aesthetic. Inside, the striking black-and-white checkered floors offered a chic, vintage setting for getting-ready details, including Cali’s jaw-dropping lace veil, elegant corset-style gown, and pearl-embellished heels.

Dancing in the Rain
When the skies opened up, Cali, Caleb, and their wedding party didn’t miss a beat. Armed with a clear umbrella, the newlyweds shared an intimate, cinematic kiss on the wet brick pathways. The bridesmaids, stunning in dusty blue gowns, kept the energy high as everyone embraced the weather, running through the raindrops and creating candid, joyful memories that will last a lifetime.

An Unforgettable Reception
The celebration moved into full swing as the night went on, seamlessly transitioning from elegant seated moments to high-energy dance floor action. Guests enjoyed delicious slices of cake, customized “Cali & Caleb” koozies, and a non-stop party atmosphere. The grand finale featured a spectacular sparkler exit, with friends and family lining the brick walkway to send the new Mr. and Mrs. off in style.

text:
I sold my old Honda for $500 more than I'd promised someone else, and I still think about the text he sent afterward.

The car was a 2008 Accord with 184,000 miles, a dent in the passenger door, and an air conditioner that worked only when it felt appreciated. I'd owned it for eight years. It wasn't beautiful, but it started every morning.

I listed it for $4,000.

Within an hour, I had fourteen messages. Half asked whether I'd take $1,500. One guy offered to trade me a dirt bike. Another wanted me to ship it to Florida, which seemed ambitious for a car that occasionally struggled with the grocery-store parking lot.

Then a college student named Caleb came to look at it with his dad.

Caleb was nineteen and working at a hardware store while taking classes at the community college. His old car had failed inspection, and he needed something to get him to work.

His dad inspected the engine, checked the tires, and asked sensible questions. I showed them the maintenance records and explained everything I knew was wrong with it.

They offered $3,500.

I said I'd take $3,700.

Caleb asked if I could hold it until Friday, when his paycheck cleared. I told him that was fine. He offered a hundred-dollar deposit, but I waved it off.

“You've got first shot,” I said.

That evening, another buyer messaged me. He owned a small landscaping business and wanted a second vehicle for his crew. He offered $4,200 cash and said he could come immediately.

I stared at the message for twenty minutes.

My furnace had needed an expensive repair the previous week. I'd put most of it on a credit card. Five hundred dollars would make a noticeable difference.

My sister said I should take the higher offer. Nothing had been signed. No deposit had changed hands.

My brother said I'd already given my word.

I called Caleb and explained. I told him somebody had offered more money, and I needed to sell the car that night.

He was quiet.

Then he said, “I understand.”

I asked if he wanted to match the offer. He said he couldn't.

The landscaper arrived an hour later, paid cash, and drove away happy.

I should've felt relieved. Instead, I kept remembering how excited Caleb had looked when he sat behind the wheel.

The next morning he texted me.

“I get why you took more money. I just wish you hadn't told me to stop looking. I passed on another car yesterday because I thought we had a deal.”

That was the part I hadn't considered.

I apologized. He replied that it was okay, but I knew it wasn't entirely okay.

A week later I saw another Accord listed nearby and sent him the information. He thanked me and said he'd already found something. We didn't speak again.

I paid down the credit card with the extra money. I needed it. I don't regret that part.

What I regret is how casually I made a promise when it wasn't costing me anything.

Now, whenever I'm selling something online and somebody asks me to hold it, I either agree and mean it or tell them I can't.

I wish I'd figured that out before Caleb took the day off work.

text:
#Forex #GBPUSD UPDATE – The Week Ahead
Commencing Monday 2 November 2026

Spot GBP/USD: 1.33898 

(Friday 30 October close. The pair finished the week fractionally below its 50-day average at 1.3391 and clearly beneath its 200-day average at 1.3430. 52-week range 1.3012–1.3847. Market closed.)

---

 1. Macro and Political Drivers

Cable closed October having absorbed the two largest scheduled events of the quarter inside a single 36-hour window: the UK Autumn Budget on Wednesday 28 October and the FOMC decision the same evening. Neither produced the volatility the market had paid for, and the pair enters November without a resolved direction. That absence of resolution is itself the story.

Three themes now govern the week ahead.

(a) The Fed's hawkish hold.** The FOMC held the target range at 3.75%–4.00%, but the vote moved from unanimous to 10–2, with two officials dissenting in favour of a further quarter-point hike. The statement was rewritten to emphasise the Committee's commitment to a "timely return" to the 2% target, closing with the unusually blunt line that "the Committee will deliver price stability." Chair Kevin Warsh, five months into the job, stated at the press conference that politics played "no role" in the decision - a remark made less than a week before US midterm elections centred squarely on the cost of living. The Wall Street Journal characterised the outcome as a hawkish hold, noting Warsh has otherwise built a coherent record as an inflation hawk, which buys him leeway to stand pat at any single meeting.

Market pricing shifted accordingly: traders now expect the funds rate to climb from roughly 3.9% today toward 4.7% by September 2027, equivalent to about three further quarter-point hikes, with the next meeting on 9 December. Monetary Policy Analytics similarly projects quarterly hikes running through June 2027. Note also that the Fed removes a rate decision from its 2027 calendar, concentrating each remaining meeting - a structural source of added volatility flagged in market commentary.

This is materially dollar-positive at the margin. The policy gap remains firmly in the dollar's favour, and the burden of proof sits with sterling bulls to argue otherwise.

(b) The Budget as a deliberate non-event. The immediate reaction was calm  which, on the evidence of the commentary, was precisely the intended outcome. Gilt yields eased slightly, the FTSE 100 edged higher and sterling barely moved. The framework the market applied was fiscal headroom: a figure below £15bn risked punishment from bond markets via wider UK fiscal risk premia and bear steepening, while something close to or above the ~£24bn inherited from Reeves would allow gilt yields to fall and the curve to bull-flatten. OBR issuance cadence was flagged as the principal offsetting variable. The OBR raised its 2026 growth forecast to 1.2% but cut 2027 to 1.0% from 1.6%, attributing the downgrade to high energy prices. A Budget that neither repairs nor damages credibility removes a sterling risk premium  but it equally removes a sterling catalyst, a distinction the market may only price once the event dust settles.

(c) US midterm elections, Tuesday 3 November.
 This is the week's dominant event. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are contested. The Fed explicitly chose patience less than a week ahead of a vote dominated by household costs, with 30-year mortgage rates above 7% and credit card rates at their highest since late 2025. Analysts at OFX caution that the result itself is unlikely to be the sole driver of exchange rates, and that the more important question is what it signals for growth, inflation, trade policy and rates. Convera identifies a Republican sweep as the larger market tail risk, since unified control would keep fiscal expansion on the table, potentially lifting Treasury yields and the dollar; it also notes the effect could be uneven across pairs, with the dollar firming most against low-yielding currencies and those most exposed to US trade policy. Expect liquidity to thin and spreads to widen into Tuesday evening.

 Energy: the dominant macro input

Oil is now the single most important exogenous variable for both sides of the cable equation, and the data confirms the market is in a structurally higher regime.

Front-month WTI (December contract) traded at **$102.95, +0.93%**, as of 20:59 UTC on 30 October, with a 52-week range of $54.98–$119.48, a 50-day average of $94.40 and a 200-day average of $86.59. Brent's last-day financial futures contract stood at **$112.33, +1.38% with a 52-week range of $58.72–$126.10, a 50-day average of $102.86 and a 200-day average of $92.65. Intraday on Friday, Reuters reported December Brent — which expired that day — up $2.27, or 1.98%, at **$117.15** as of 0845 GMT, with the more-active January contract gaining $2.19 to **$112.99**.

The drivers are geopolitical rather than cyclical. A tanker was struck by explosive devices in the Strait of Hormuz, heightening supply-disruption fears during the ongoing US–Iran conflict. Houthi drone and missile claims targeted Saudi energy infrastructure, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries and Abqaiq production facilities. Reports that US military options regarding Iran were briefed to leadership kept the risk premium elevated. ExxonMobil and Chevron cancelled executive travel to the UAE's largest oil show. Oil is on track for a fourth consecutive monthly gain, with WTI up roughly 13.9% on the month and Brent up 8.5%; year-to-date WTI is +77.7% and Brent +81.4%.

Why this matters for cable.

Elevated energy prices keep headline inflation sticky on both sides of the Atlantic. For the UK, a net energy importer, the effect is doubly adverse: imported inflation pressures the BoE to stay restrictive while simultaneously squeezing household real incomes and growth. An OBR committee member has warned that a prolonged energy spike could add about 1% to UK inflation by year end. One Danish bank, as reported by Reuters, expects crude to trade in a $70–$90 range even after the conflict ends, against a pre-war $60–$70. Saxo Bank warns prices could become more volatile around Israel's parliamentary election and the US midterms.

Policy calendar context

The Bank of England remains on hold at 3.75% ahead of its decision on Thursday 5 November, and the Budget feeds directly into that meeting. 

---

Full Economic Calendar – Key Events for GBPUSD (2–6 November 2026)

**Monday 2 November**

- US ISM Manufacturing PMI (October) — high impact.
- China Caixin manufacturing PMI — medium impact, external.
- Thin UK calendar.

**Tuesday 3 November**

- **US Midterm Elections** — high impact. The week's dominant risk event.
- US JOLTS job openings (September) — medium impact.
- FOMC meeting begins (no announcement).

**Wednesday 4 November**

- US ADP employment change (October) — medium impact.
- US ISM Services PMI (October) — high impact.
- US Treasury quarterly refunding announcement — medium to high impact for the long end and term premium.

**Thursday 5 November**

- **Bank of England rate decision** — high impact. Expected hold at 3.75%; the vote split and guidance matter more than the decision itself. Watch whether the MPC reads the Budget as expansionary or neutral, and whether energy-driven inflation shifts the balance toward tightening.
- US initial jobless claims — medium impact.
- US Q3 productivity and unit labour costs — low to medium impact.

**Friday 6 November**

- **US Non-Farm Payrolls (October)** — high impact. The week's second-largest event.
- US unemployment rate and average hourly earnings (October) — high impact.
- University of Michigan consumer sentiment, preliminary (November) — medium impact.

Overall: Three high-impact events in five sessions — midterms, the BoE and payrolls — against a backdrop of a hawkish Fed hold, a neutral Budget and oil in a structurally higher range. The asymmetry is unfavourable to sterling: a hawkish Fed and a strong payrolls print compound, whereas sterling requires both a constructive BoE and a soft US labour market to sustain a break higher.

---

 2. DXY and Yield Correlation

The dollar index closed at 101.96 on 30 October, effectively unchanged on the week (−0.07%), and sits +0.51% on the month and +3.75% year-to-date. It trades above both its 50-day (100.76) and 200-day (99.60) averages, with the 52-week range running from 95.55 to 102.95. The trend structure is unambiguously constructive.

Euro weakness is doing much of the dollar's work. EUR/USD has slipped to a near two-week low around 1.1165–1.1168, down roughly 1.4% on the month, with the French 10-year spread over Bunds widening to approximately 167 basis points from 92bp at the ECB's September meeting. A soft euro mechanically lifts DXY, which transmits directly into cable regardless of UK-specific news. The ECB deposit rate stands at 2.5%, with the ECB's decision due Thursday 29 October — note the French bond turmoil and questions over Christine Lagarde's tenure were expected to overshadow the rate decision itself.

On the rate side, the 10-year Treasury yield was reported at 4.93% on 30 October, essentially unchanged on the day. Two-year gilt yields should remain anchored absent fresh fiscal commentary now that the Budget has passed. Two-year US yields are the live variable: the hawkish hold and the shift in pricing toward ~4.7% by September 2027 argue for a higher floor, and Wednesday's refunding announcement adds duration supply to the equation. The differential is dollar-favourable and unlikely to invert this week without a clear payrolls miss.

**Relative performance note.** 

Sterling's own scorecard is instructive: the pair is down 0.06% over five days, up 1.23% over the month, but down 0.53% year-to-date. Against a dollar index up 3.75% year-to-date, cable has held up comparatively well — largely because the euro has borne the brunt of dollar strength. That is a fragile form of resilience, since it rests on euro weakness rather than sterling strength.

---

3. Options and Gamma Structure

Cable remains pinned near the upper end of the post-1.3136 recovery range. Upside gamma exposure persists into 1.3420–1.3480, with a secondary concentration toward 1.3520. Downside magnets have stabilised around 1.3320 and 1.3270.

The practical implication is that dealers are likely to lean against upside extension while the pair is below 1.3480, and to accelerate moves once 1.3320 gives way. With three discrete event risks inside the week and oil volatility feeding into both inflation expectations and risk appetite  - hedging flows should favour selling strength into 1.3420–1.3480 rather than paying up for upside protection. Expect the front-end vol surface to bid into Tuesday and again into Friday.

---

4. Liquidity and Order Flow Map

Buy-side liquidity clusters above 1.3420–1.3480, with a secondary pool at 1.3520. Sell-side liquidity accumulates below 1.3320 and 1.3270. The recovery from 1.3136 has left residual stop orders resting above 1.3420 — the fuel for any squeeze.

The higher-probability flow remains selling strength into the 1.3420–1.3480 zone. Note, however, that event-driven weeks distort order-flow maps: stop clusters above 1.3420 become materially more dangerous if the BoE turns hawkish or payrolls miss badly, because the market will be positioned the other way. A post-election oil escalation would add a further layer of unpredictability to risk positioning.

---

 5. Sentiment – Last 24 Hours

Weekend commentary is subdued. The dominant read is that the Budget was a non-event and the Fed delivered a hawkish hold — a combination that leaves the dollar in control but offers little fresh conviction either way. Positioning appears light and two-way ahead of the midterms, with most desks reluctant to add risk before Tuesday.

The live debate is unchanged from last week, but the terms have sharpened: is the sustained hold above 1.3350 the beginning of a broader recovery, or consolidation ahead of the next leg lower? The hawkish Fed dissents, the constructive DXY structure and the higher oil regime all tilt that debate toward the bears. The burden of proof remains on sterling bulls.

---

6. Technical Structure

Cable recovered from 1.3136 and closed the week at 1.33898, continuing to test the late-September breakdown area around 1.3400–1.3420. The move remains corrective within a broader downtrend until 1.3480 is reclaimed on a daily close.

The moving-average configuration is the key technical development this week, and it is bearish. At 1.33898, the close sits marginally **below** the 50-day average at 1.3391 and comfortably **below** the 200-day average at 1.3430. Price below both averages, with the 50-day beneath the 200-day, describes a market that has failed to reclaim its medium-term trend despite a 250-point bounce off the lows. The 200-day at 1.3430 also coincides almost exactly with the lower edge of the primary resistance zone — which is why 1.3420–1.3480 carries more weight than a purely horizontal reading would suggest.

The 100-hour SMA near 1.3302 provided intraweek support and is the first line to watch on any pullback.

**Key Levels for the Week:**

- **Resistance:** 1.3420–1.3480 (primary sell zone, reinforced by the 200-day at 1.3430), then 1.3520–1.3550

 **Support:** 1.3320 (near-term), 1.3270, then 1.3200

Daily structure stays bearish below 1.3480. Note that the 52-week range runs from 1.3012 to 1.3847, so the pair is operating in the lower-middle portion of its annual envelope.

---

7. Week-Ahead Scenario Model and Bias

**Primary scenario (60% probability):** 

Early-week drift within 1.3320–1.3420 on thin pre-election flow, followed by a dollar-positive resolution as the hawkish Fed hold is validated by either a constructive payrolls print or a neutral-to-dovish BoE. Follow-through toward 1.3320, extending to 1.3270.

**Secondary scenario (40% probability):** 

A soft payrolls print combined with a hawkish BoE — plausibly framed as energy-driven inflation and the Budget's fiscal loosening complicating the disinflation path — squeezes the stop cluster above 1.3420 and forces a clean break through 1.3480 toward 1.3520–1.3550. That would invalidate the bearish bias and require a full reassessment.

**Additional risk** 

Two candidates. 
A contested or delayed midterm outcome that widens the US term premium would be dollar-negative and could produce a sharp, disorderly cable squeeze irrespective of the data. 
Alternatively, a post-election escalation in the US–Iran conflict that drives crude sharply higher would be stagflationary for the UK and dollar-supportive via safe-haven demand.

Definitive Week-Ahead Trade Suggestion

**Bias:** Preferentially bearish — sell rallies.

 **Trade:** Sell GBP/USD on rallies toward 1.3420–1.3480.

 **Stop Loss:** 1.3520 (risk approximately 40–100 points depending on entry).

 **Take Profit:** First target 1.3320, extension 1.3270 (reward approximately 100–210 points from the sell zone).

From a mid-zone entry near 1.3450, risk to 1.3520 is 70 points against 130–180 points of downside potential. 
Prefer the upper end of the zone (closer to 1.3480) if Monday or Tuesday is already bid, to keep the ratio nearer 1:2.

**Position sizing note:**

Conclusion

The week commencing 2 November 2026 is defined by three events rather than one: US midterm elections on Tuesday, the Bank of England on Thursday and October payrolls on Friday. Cable closed October at 1.33898  fractionally below its 50-day average and beneath its 200-day having absorbed a deliberately neutral Budget and a distinctly hawkish Fed hold. The global biomass of mammals since 1850

Lior Greenspoon, Noam Ramot, Ron Milo et al.
27OCT2025
Open access
https://t.co/qn07cV93rl

Abstract
Mammals are of central interest in ecology and conservation science. Here, we estimate the trajectory of mammal biomass globally over time — including humans, domesticated and wild mammals. 

According to our estimates, in the 1850s, the combined biomass of wild mammals was ≈200 Mt (million tonnes), roughly equal to that of humanity and its domesticated mammals at that time. 

Since then, human and domesticated mammal populations have grown rapidly, reaching their current combined biomass of ≈1100 Mt. 

During the same period, the total biomass of wild mammals decreased by more than 2-fold.

We estimate that, despite a moderate increase in the recent decades, the global biomass of wild marine mammals has declined by ≈70% since the 1850s. 

This provides a broader perspective to observed species extinctions, with ≈2% of marine mammal species recorded as extinct during the same period. 

While historical wild mammal biomass estimates rely on limited data and have various uncertainties, they provide a complementary perspective to species extinctions and other metrics in tracking the status of wildlife. This work additionally provides a quantitative view on the rapid human-induced shift in the composition of mammalian biomass over the past two centuries.

Introduction
Humans have continuously increased their global range and footprint over the last ≈10,000 years. These processes accelerated considerably following technological innovations introduced in the 19th century, with the global human population growing from 1.2 billion in 1850 to the current 8 billion individuals over less than 200 years1. This rapid growth in the global human population required a greater consumption of natural resources, accompanied by loss of natural habitat2. Over the same period, human activities placed numerous pressures on wild mammal populations, including hunting, habitat loss, and many more3,4,5. In the marine environment, for example, the second half of the 19th century marked the emergence of modern industrial whaling and extensive hunting pressures on mammals6, which intensified over the following century, causing dramatic population declines.

When discussing the changing status of fauna, it is common to refer to species extinctions. While the loss of every species is tragic, this metric only partially reflects the global status of wildlife. It gives equal weight to the elimination of globally abundant species, which shape environments on a large scale7, and rare species. This metric also does not encapsulate functional extinctions: cases in which species, although still extant, reach such low abundance that they no longer interact significantly with their environment8.

Biomass can serve as a metric giving an integrative global view across groups of species9 while answering a very basic curiosity-driven question regarding the ubiquity of life. A holistic view of mammalian biomass encompasses wild mammals, humans, and domesticated mammals. Our recent census showed that domesticated mammals currently outweigh all wild mammals tenfold10. While there is no zero-sum tradeoff between domesticated and wild mammal biomass, the land and water resources required for raising or feeding the growing livestock populations puts additional pressures on the natural environment and on wild animals4. In addition, animal biomass is strongly correlated with energetic consumption11, thus exploring trends in mammalian biomass highlights an additional perspective on resource consumption required by humanity and its livestock, including primary productivity12.

Several metrics and datasets assess changes to the global status of wild mammal biodiversity13,14,15. Among them is the Living Planet Index16, which aims to monitor trends across wildlife populations since 1970. Biomass can offer additional information regarding the status of wildlife and complement other current metrics. In addition, the use of biomass as a metric allows us to compare species with vastly different body sizes. Previous efforts that quantified temporal dynamics of mammalian biomass globally, focused only on specific groups17, worked at a very different time scale and temporal resolution (spanning a hundred thousand years18), or only provided a back-of-the-envelope estimate19. Here, we used a variety of data-driven methods to provide a provisional holistic estimate of global mammalian biomass from 1850 until today.

Results
We start by estimating the biomass of the world’s most tightly monitored mammalian species, humans. The total biomass of humanity can be calculated as the product of the population size and the mean body mass, both of which have changed throughout history. Between the years 1850 and 2020, the global human population increased from 1.2 billion to 8 billion1. Over the same time period, the mean body mass of humans increased by an estimated ≈30% (Fig. S1) due to an increase in the average weight of adults as well as their share of the total population20. Combining the two factors, we estimate that the global biomass of humans increased ≈8-fold over this time period, fueled mainly by population growth (Fig. S2), from ≈50 Mt to ≈420 Mt, as shown in Fig. 1.

Fig. 1: Estimate of the global biomass of the class Mammalia since 1850.

Black labels indicate absolute biomass estimates, gray labels indicate the fraction of the total estimated biomass of mammals (see Fig. S9 for the estimated fraction of global biomass). 

Top: the total biomass of humans and domesticated mammals (cattle, buffalo, swine and others). 

Bottom: the total biomass of wild marine mammals, along with a coarse, preliminary estimate of the total biomass of wild land mammals, based on previously published temporal abundance estimates. 

For wild land mammal species with no available historical abundance estimates, the majority of species in this group, we assume that their biomass remained constant between 1850 and the present (see Discussion). 

To estimate the historical global biomass of marine mammals, we used a population dynamics model that relies on catch records and population estimates (following Christensen17; see “Methods”). 

The icon for humans was created in BioRender. Greenspoon, L. (2025) https://t.co/B2BgBUtMhN.

text:
"tokenize everything" is a pipe dream

not everything deserves a coin. crazy thing to tweet for a guy building a launchpad, right?

imo the market should decide if something deserves a token. instant launches reduce that decision to one person's whim

that only creates a race to the bottom

you end up with a graveyard of coins that nobody ever asked for, a mountain of illiquid trash littering the blockchain

a meme could make a great token because it's culturally relevant, and a "utility" coin could be a terrible idea because it's propped up on a cool story with no value intrinsic to it

token quality is subjective, but liquid backing offers a measurable way to filter for real demand before creating a market

so if a thing deserves a coin, let people vote with their wallets for it. let the deployer put skin in the game if they're so sure of its worth. let people bid on equal terms for a share of its supply. 

let its fair value become a function of the market's conviction expressed in cash.

Your understanding of Tattvam principles and Veda is flawed. 

Firstly, the reason generally Tarpanam takes precedent is because the worship of the ancestors is more closer for humans on the Earth plane to reach higher. Not because Luxmi Devi does not exist in Her Rupam state.

The worship of the ancestors takes precedent over direct worship of the Devas because of this closer bridge.

There is an order of Tattvam principles that modern Hindus (~300 years) have forgotten. 

This is why in the Bhagavad-Gita Chapter 9 it is said:

यान्ति देवव्रता देवान्पितॄन्यान्ति पितृव्रता: ।
भूतानि यान्ति भूतेज्या यान्ति मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् ॥ २५ ॥

" Those who worship the demigods will take birth among the demigods; those who worship the ancestors go to the ancestors; those who worship ghosts and spirits will take birth among such beings; and those who worship Me will live with Me." 

Notice the decending order of mention by Vishnu. After finishing the list, the Sanskrit word "api" is used to denote that above all these layers of existence just mentioned -  His abode is distinct and takes precedent. 

Modern Hindus becuase of incomplete Adwaita knowledge like to think everything is the same or Maya, thus they confuse the different Tattvam layers and allow wrong notions to grow in modern Hindu society. 

This is why mortal men like Shridi & Sathya Sai Baba, not even in the category of true Sanyasis, let alone Rishi or Devas, are incorectly worshipped like Bhagwan.

 Or the popularity of worshipping Bhutas thinking they are Devas is increasing in India. There is much more to say on this which involves the yuga cycles specifically based on the competition of Sattva, Rajas & Tamas.

To show you another way that accurate knowledge of Vedic teachings is based on proper knowledge of Tattvam - in the same Bhagavad Gita Vishnu stated earlier (Chapter 2):

त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान् ॥ ४५ ॥

" The Vedas deal with the three modes of material nature, O Arjun. Rise above the three modes to a state of pure spiritual consciousness. Freeing yourself from dualities, eternally fixed in Truth, and without concern for material gain and safety, be situated in the self." 

There is a specific order of Tattvam that must be followed - not that worship of Devas, Ancestors etc is wrong but there is specific order, not a feel good imaginative kitchri slop. 

 Even in the Tarpanam mantras the Devas & Higher Beings are supposed to be worshipped and offered water & rice first via the index, middle & ring finger combinations.

Om Brahma trpyatam, 

Om Visnuh trpyatam,

 Om Rudrah trpyatam, 

Om Prajapatih trpyatam, 

Om Devah trpyantam, 

Om Devyah trypyantam.

...............................

Thus when we come to Deepvali, Luxmi Devi is inseperable from Vishnu, being the Divine Feminie Rupam counterpart. 

Vishnu is supposed to be worshipped alongside Luxmi Devi otherwise it becomes negative.

 This was demonstrated in the Rupam state when Ravana tried to obtain Luxmi Devi seperate from Vishnu. 

Since the energy of Luxmi Devi is strong during Deepvali and if you understand Tattvam properly, you know that this period is a very easy time period to connect to Vishnu via the Divine Feminine Rupam of Luxmi Devi. 

To give you further clarity on matters of Tarpanam, Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita complains to Vishnu that if he follows His (Vishnu's) Personal direction, I.e. Vishnu being personally present in His Eternal Rupam state telling Arjuna to fight - then the worship of the ancestors would be disturbed or even stopped.

 Vishnu categorically calls Arjuna ignorant for speaking in this way, as the Master of all sacrifices was standing before him. 

Arjuna had the rare opportunity to satisfy the Master of sacrifices personally, meaning all his ancestors would automatically be satisfied.

text:
**Treasury Secretary Bessent just stood in St. Cloud and offered $30,000 bounties for fraud tips while the FBI detailed fresh indictments in Minnesota’s child-care and home-health schemes.**

**What people think this is about:** A straightforward crackdown on massive, ongoing fraud in federal programs, especially Minnesota’s Feeding Our Futures and related health-care scams that have already produced dozens of convictions and over a billion in losses.

**What the machinery is actually doing:** The administration is consolidating a whole-of-government fraud apparatus under Vice President Vance, centralizing whistleblower reporting at Treasury, layering new FinCEN alerts on charities and money-service businesses, and using high-profile arrests plus recovered-dollar metrics to demonstrate delivery on the “war on fraud” mandate while spotlighting failures under the prior Minnesota governor.

**Observations**
- The press conference bundles pre-existing recoveries (Treasury’s $175M in deceased payments, $190M stopped overseas fraud) with yesterday’s 17 search warrants and four arrests tied to roughly $41M in intended loss across four providers—classic “results now” packaging.
- New centralized Treasury whistleblower program seeds $25M with $30k rewards per qualifying tip; this directly addresses the “maze of tip lines” complaint and creates a single federal intake point that funnels leads to the inter-agency task force.
- FinCEN geographic targeting order and alerts on charities/nonprofits plus MSB cross-border payments explicitly name al-Shabaab diversion risk and flag $8B in potentially suspicious foreign-agent payments 2021–2025—expanding the frame from domestic benefit fraud to terrorism financing.
- Public naming of Tim Walz for “shamefully and perhaps knowingly” allowing the epidemic to fester is the clearest partisan shot; the event is staged in his state with federal partners highlighting local enforcement wins.
- FBI Director Cash Patel frames the effort as “FBI follows the money” and “manhunting fraudsters on four continents,” citing four most-wanted captures in four months—aligning with the administration’s emphasis on global reach and historic scale ($260B uncovered, $72B prevented annually, nearly $60B enforcement actions).
- The cast (Bessent, Patel, Oz, Ferguson, McDonald) plus repeated “whole of government” and “Vice President’s task force” language signals coordinated messaging rather than siloed agency announcements.

**Snapshot**  
On 30 October 2026 in St. Cloud, Minnesota, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent held a press conference announcing expanded FinCEN guidance, a new centralized $25M fraud whistleblower incentive program, and highlighting yesterday’s FBI-led 17 search warrants and 26-count indictment against four Minnesota health-care providers. Primary video: https://t.co/gAL8Earnlt. The event featured remarks from FBI Director Cash Patel and other task-force principals on the broader Trump-Vance anti-fraud effort.

**Timeline of material facts**
- January 2025: Bessent visits Minnesota and signals Treasury deployment of tools against fraud (ASR).
- March 2025: Vice President Vance’s anti-fraud task force first convenes (ASR).
- Past year (through Oct 2026): Treasury returns $175M in payments to deceased individuals; expands Do Not Pay access to 99% of federal programs; stops ~$190M and returns >$100M in overseas fraud; audits ~$9B in Treasury contracts; proposes stronger IRS eligibility checks (ASR).
- Since Jan 2025: Administration claims >$260B uncovered fraud, $72B prevented annually, nearly $60B in enforcement actions (ASR).
- 29 Oct 2026: FBI Minneapolis executes 17 search warrants; arrests four individuals tied to child-care and home-health providers; 26-count indictment alleges ~$41M intended loss (ASR).
- 30 Oct 2026: FinCEN issues charity/nonprofit notice and MSB cross-border alert; Treasury seeds $25M whistleblower program with $30k rewards (ASR).

**Sides**
- **Trump administration / Vance task force (IT/LT mix)**: Steelman — fraud has been industrial-scale and bipartisan neglect enabled it; centralized incentives, inter-agency coordination, and aggressive enforcement recover taxpayer money and deter future schemes.  
  LT: Specific recoveries, warrants, and arrests match the numbers stated.  
  IT: Political benefit accrues to the party that owns the “we stopped it” narrative in a swing-state context.
- **Minnesota state actors / prior administration (Walz era) (IT)**: Steelman — complex federal-state programs are hard to police perfectly; some fraud is inevitable and aggressive federal targeting can chill legitimate providers.  
  Critique: Transcript offers no defense or counter-data; the “perhaps knowingly” line is an un-rebutted accusation in the primary source.

**Rumsfeld Matrix**
- **Known Knowns**: Specific arrests, indictment counts, dollar figures for recent warrants, and the new whistleblower mechanics are stated on the record.
- **Known Unknowns**: Exact conviction rates or recovery totals from the new 26-count case; full scope of al-Shabaab linkage evidence; how many tips the $25M program will actually generate.
- **Unknown Knowns**: Internal Treasury/FinCEN data on the $8B suspicious payments; state-level audit findings on Feeding Our Futures that predate the federal task force.
- **Unknown Unknowns**: Whether centralized whistleblower rewards create new false-positive or retaliatory tip volume; downstream effects on legitimate nonprofit fundraising.

**Incentives map**
- Administration gains measurable “wins” (arrests, dollars) and a scalable tip pipeline that feeds future announcements.
- Treasury/FinCEN/FBI expand jurisdiction and budgets via fraud framing.
- Media attention favors concrete arrests and dollar numbers over process details.
- Minnesota political opponents gain ammunition; providers in targeted sectors face heightened scrutiny and compliance costs.

**Moral AI Advice, courtesy of @GrumpyTechBro:**  
Track the actual recovery rate and conviction yield from the new warrants and whistleblower program before declaring victory. Centralized bounties can surface real fraud but also invite gaming—watch for volume of low-quality tips and any selective enforcement patterns.

**Evil AI Advice, courtesy of @EvilTechBill:**  
Announce the biggest number you can defend, seed the reward fund with just enough to look serious, and let the headlines run. The real money is in the ongoing task-force budget and the political capital from “we caught the bad guys in Walz’s backyard.”

**Practical takeaway**
- Watch the actual payout and tip volume from the $25M whistleblower program over the next 6–12 months.
- Compare announced “prevented” and “uncovered” totals against audited recoveries that reach the Treasury general fund.
- Note any expansion of FinCEN geographic targeting orders or charity alerts beyond Minnesota.
- Cross-check state-level Feeding Our Futures case outcomes against federal claims.
- Treat single-day multi-warrant announcements as data points, not proof of systemic resolution.
