text:
The Origins of Surnames for Antebellum-Black Americans in the Antebellum Era

According to the 1860 US Census, there were 488,070 free Antebellum-Black / Antebellum-Moor Americans in the USA just before the Civil War began in 1861 (roughly 488,000 to 500,000 people, making up about 11% of the total Black population). These individuals already had first, middle, and last names. Many were landowners & business owners, some owned slaves themselves, some were citizens and fewer had the right to vote in the Northern or non-slave states.

Regional Distribution
Total Free Antebellum-Black Population: 488,070
Free States (North): 226,152 (approx. 46.3%)
Slave States (South & Border States): 261,918 (approx. 53.7%), with a large majority of Southern free Antebellum-Black residents living in the Upper South (such as Virginia and Maryland) rather than the Lower South.

When the 13th Amendment abolished slavery in 1865, approximately four million formerly enslaved individuals gained the legal right to choose their own surnames. Prior to the 1870 US Census, the first federal census to record formerly enslaved or Antebellum-Black Americans by name rather than as unnamed property statistics, naming practices were incredibly fluid.

A common historical misconception is that most freed people automatically adopted the last name of their final enslaver. In reality, historians and genealogists note that roughly 80% of Antebellum-Black Americans chose or "made up" new surnames to intentionally break ties with their most recent oppressors, protect themselves, or freely declare their new identities.

During the Antebellum Era, the enslaved generally did not have official, legally recognized surnames. They were typically known only by a first name.
Freed Black individuals & families, whether they gained freedom through manumission or escape between the 1600s & the US Civil War, chose or inherited surnames through a variety of personal, familial, and practical methods rather than simply adopting the names of their former enslavers.
Surnames only became a widespread necessity after emancipation (the end of the Civil War & the 13th Amendment), when newly freed Antebellum-Black / Antebellum-Moor Americans) registered for marriages, land, employment & the 1870 US Census.

How Surnames Were Chosen
-Patronymics and Ancestral Names: Many Antebellum-Black Americans adopted the first name of a father, grandfather, or respected family elder as a surname to honor family ties and signal lineage such as John, James, Henry, Roberts, Thomas.
Johnson (Literally "Son of John", widely adopted to cement family lineages) -Williams (Derived from "Son of William") -Brown (Simple English surname widely used to denote family branches) -Jones (Derived from John or Jonas, highly utilized across the South) -Thomas (Elevating a paternal given name to a last name) -Harris (Derived from Harry or Harrison) -Robinson (Derived from Robert or Robin)
-Robert/Robertson (Derived from Robert) -Davis (Derived from David, sometimes used to adapt secret family lines)
-Henry (Reclaiming a common ancestral first name)
-James (Reclaiming a common ancestral first name) -Lewis (Reclaiming a common ancestral first name) -Allen (Adopted as a family identifier) -Walker (Often tied to ancestral lines or symbolic of moving away from bondage) -Scott (Frequently used as a traditional family name passed down orally during slavery) -Young (Used to distinguish younger generations establishing new lines)
-Declarations of Status: Freed people frequently "made up" surnames based on local landscapes, regions, or words associated with royalty & personal dignity to replace the humiliating classical names (like Caesar or Jupiter), Names like:
Freeman (Literally declaring a "free man")
Freedman (Marking the transition from enslavement to liberty)
Liberty (Chosen to celebrate emancipation)
Justice (Reflecting the hope for a fair society)
Hope (Chosen as a forward-looking family marker)
Independence (Adopted to assert self-reliance)
King or Queen (A status name chosen to assert dignity, honor, and self-worth)
Prince (Selected to project high regard
White (Sometimes chosen adaptively to blend into records or camouflage identity for protection)
-Aspirational and Historical Figures:
Many Antebellum-Black Americans selected names of foundational figures, military leaders, or prominent abolitionists to align their new families with national ideals or symbols of freedom, prestige and dignity.

-Washington (The absolute most common surname chosen by freed people, chosen to honor the country's ideals or mark survival) -Lincoln (In honor of Abraham Lincoln and the Emancipation Proclamation) -Jackson (Often associated with Andrew Jackson or adopted from Southern prominence) -Jefferson (Highly concentrated among Black Americans, linked to Thomas Jefferson) -Grant (To honor Union General and President Ulysses S. Grant) -Douglass (Deliberately taken to honor the legendary abolitionist Frederick Douglass) -Franklin (Inspired by Benjamin Franklin or chosen for its linguistic association with being a "free landholder") -Madison (Inspired by James Madison) -Monroe (Inspired by James Monroe) -Clay (Often selected due to political prominence) -Lee (Widespread in the South, frequently adopted or adapted)
-Occupational & Craft Names: Antebellum-Black Americans who possessed highly specialized skills used their trade to create their new family identity. During slavery, their labor belonged to someone else; in freedom, they chose to own the title of their expertise.
Names tied to trades & skills, such as
-Smith (Commonly adopted by plantation blacksmiths who held high communal value)
-Miller  (Operators of grain and lumber mills)
-Farmer (Emphasizing a family's new connection to working their own crops)
-Green (Often occupational for groundskeepers or symbolic of new growth)
-Gardener (Cultivators of land and botanical skills)
-Parker  (Keeper or warden of a park)
-Carter (Derived from cart drivers or transporters)
-Cooper (Barrel makers, a vital skilled trade in the Antebellum era)
-Mason (Stonemasons and builders)
-Carpenter (Woodworkers & structural builders)
-Cook (Reflecting culinary mastery)
-Turner (Lathe operators or wood-turners, also associated with Nat Turner's rebellion)
-Taylor / Tailor (Adopted by skilled clothes makers and seamstresses)
-Shepherd / Sheperd (Livestock handlers & caretakers)
-Wright (Craftsman or woodworker)
-Barber (Haircutter, surgeon, or tooth-puller)
-Tanner (Leather tanner)
-Fuller (Scourer & thickener of raw cloth)
-Dyer (Dyeing cloth specialist)
-Collier (Coal or charcoal burner/seller)
-Silver (Silver smith or worker)
-Weaver (Cloth weaver)
-Baxter (Female or traditional baker)
-Webster Female cloth weaver (later general weaver)
Chapman, Chandler, Coach  Author, Butcher, Baker, Fisher, Hunter, Sailor, Cutter, Hammer, Page, Bishop, Elder, Potter, Goldsmith, Barker, Waller, Chamberlin, Butler, Fletcher, were adopted to reflect a person's competence, livelihood, and standing in the community.
-Geographical & Land-Based Names: Individuals selected names based on local geography, towns, counties, rivers, or agricultural life (such as Banks, Hill, Marsh, Clay, Fields, Woods, Brook, Ford, Bridge, Stone, Lane, Shore, Camp, Rivers, Lake, Lee / Leigh, Holmes, Hall, Grove, Underwood, Forest, Moore, Heath, Dike, Ash, Bailey, Cross, Burton, Cliff or specific place names) to anchor their identity to a physical place rather than a master.
-Ordinary or Blend-in Names: Common English or Anglo-American surnames like Pearce, Johnson, Williams, Brown, and Jones were chosen to integrate smoothly into the broader community and offer a degree of everyday safety or anonymity.
-Former Enslaver Surnames (Selective): While some freed individuals did keep the surname of a past or current enslaver for continuity or to help locate scattered family members from the same plantation, historian research (such as that by Herbert Gutman) shows this was often linked to an older plantation where the family unit was last intact, or rejected entirely once true legal autonomy arrived.
-Colonial & Creole Heritages: In regions like Louisiana, free people of color (gens de couleur libres) often carried French (Dubois, Dumas, Duvall, Fontaine or Spanish (Rios, Silva, Bettencourt) surnames dating back to the 1700s, documented extensively through church and notarial records.
-While many people assume that Antebellum-Black Americans exclusively hold English last names, surnames of Irish ( Bryant, Carroll, Lynch, or Sullivan) , German and Dutch (  Schumacher/Shoemaker, Van Buren, Schuyler, Meyers, Hoffman, or Linker), Welsh and Scottish (Campbell, Mcintosh, Pierce, Piers, Gordon, Grant, Scott, Jones, Williams, and Evans) are highly prevalent.
-Paternal Ancestry and Coercion
DNA & genealogical evidence show a significant divergence between chosen surnames & biological ancestry, heavily rooted in the exploitation of enslaved Antebellum-Moorena. White overseers, plantation owners, and neighboring laborers of Irish, Scottish, or German descent frequently fathered children with enslaved women through coercion and rape. In the Reconstruction period, some individuals chose to take the surname of their biological father, even if he was white and had never legally recognized them.
-Integration: In urban areas during both the antebellum era (for free Antebellum-Black populations) and Reconstruction/Postbellum eras 1865 - 1945, Antebellum-Black/Anglo-Black/Anglo-Moor Americans lived & worked alongside working-class Irish & German immigrants. Surnames were occasionally adopted through close social ties, community integration, or intermarriage within these working-class neighborhoods.
-Institutional & Bureaucratic Assignment
During the antebellum period, if an enslaved person was manumitted (freed), or during the Reconstruction era when registering to vote, signing labor contracts, or applying for Civil War pensions, the federal government or local courts required a full legal name. If an individual did not have a surname, or if a census taker or Freedman's Bureau officer couldn't understand or spell their preferred name, a European surname common to the local area (such as a local German or Irish name) was often assigned to them on official paperwork.
How Surnames Were Chosen World Wide
-Surnames developed across these cultures & regions through a mix of medieval administration, religious edicts, tax registries, and 19th-to-20th-century state modernization laws.
China
Ancient Origins: Chinese surnames date back thousands of years & originally had two components: Xing (姓), which were ancient matrilineal clan names, and Shi (氏), which were patrilineal branch or status names.
Patrilineal Shift: Over time, Xing and Shi merged, and surnames became strictly patrilineal, passed down from father to child to emphasize lineage and imperial organization.
Common Names: Most surnames are monosyllabic (Wang, Li, Zhang) and often trace back to ancient feudal states, professions, or aristocratic titles. Women traditionally kept their maiden names after marriage.
Italy
Northern Beginnings: Hereditary surnames first appeared around the 9th & 10th centuries in trading hubs like Venice and northern Italy, driven by urban growth and commerce.
Spread South: The practice moved southwards over the next 500 years, standardizing completely after the 16th century. Common patterns include patronymics, pluralized endings (-i, Rossi), and regional occupational or nickname roots.
Spain
Patronymic Endings: Many Spanish surnames originated as patronymics marked by the suffix -ez (meaning "son of"), such as Rodríguez (son of Rodrigo) or González (son of Gonzalo).
Consolidation: Emerging during the Middle Ages, surnames spread from nobility to commoners for tax and property tracking, eventually becoming fixed hereditary multi-part surnames (combining paternal and maternal lines)
England
Norman Conquest (1066): The ruling Norman elite introduced hereditary surnames to track feudal landholdings and tax obligations.
Diffusion: Surnames trickled down to the general population through the 13th–15th centuries. They generally fall into four buckets: topographic (Hill), locative (Atwood), occupational (Smith), and patronymic (Johnson, prefixed with Mac- or Fitz-)
Germany
Urban & Regional Growth: German family names (Familiennamen) began emerging around the 12th century in southern & urban centers, solidifying northward through the 16th century.
Four Main Types: Berufsnamen (Occupational, Müller [miller] or Schneider [tailor]) Übernamen (Nicknames/physical traits, Klein, Schwarz) Herkunfts-/Wohnstättenamen (Geographic or landscape origins, Bergmann, Bauer) Vatersnamen (Patronymics like Peters or Albrecht)
France
Aristocracy to Commoners: Noble families adopted "de + place name" starting in the 11th century to mark land ownership.
State Registration: The practice trickled down to commoners over the next few centuries and became legally anchored when the Council of Trent (1563) and royal decrees by King Francis I mandated parish baptismal and civil records.
Jews
Early Origins: Scholars and prominent individuals in North Africa, Spain, France, and Italy used non-hereditary patronymics, occupational, or toponymic names as early as the 10th and 11th centuries.
Sephardic Tradition: Exiles from Spain and Portugal (1492/1496) carried fixed Iberian surnames ( Toledano, Alves, Abravanel) across North Africa, the Ottoman Empire, and Europe.
Ashkenazi Mandate: In Central and Eastern Europe, most families did not have permanent surnames until government decrees forced them to adopt German-style names, such as Austria’s Patent über die Judennamen issued by Joseph II in 1787 and similar laws in the Russian Empire. Common endings include -berg, -stein, and -witz.
Arabs
The Nasab System: Traditional Arabic naming uses a chain of patronymics (ibn or bin meaning "son of"; bint meaning "daughter of"), alongside a kunya (honorific "father/mother of") and a nisba (denoting tribe, region, or craft).
Hereditary Surnames: Fixed family names (ism al-usra) expanded significantly under late Ottoman administration, Western colonial influences, and 19th-to-20th-century national civil registries. Many start with the definite article Al- (Al-Masri, Al-Husseini).
Scandinavia:
Many Scandinavian regions did not adopt fixed hereditary surnames until the 18th & 19th centuries.
Korea
Aristocratic Privilege: Historically, surnames were restricted to the royalty and nobility (Yangban), while the general population (commoners and slaves) did not have formal family names.
Dynastic Continuity: Unlike many other regions where shifting dynasties wiped out old ruling families, Korea’s peaceful dynastic transitions (Silla, Goryeo, Joseon) allowed core ruling lineages like Kim, Lee (Yi), and Park to maintain & spread their names.
Universal Adoption: Surnames became universal for all citizens during the Gabo Reforms in 1894, allowing commoners to adopt names (often purchasing them or taking the names of local patrons/clans), leading to a heavy concentration of a few major surnames. Each surname is tied to an ancestral seat.
Japan
Samurai vs. Commoners: For most of Japanese history, hereditary family surnames were reserved for the samurai, nobility, and upper classes. Commoners typically used only personal names or identified themselves by their village, occupation, or house.
The 1875 Mandate: Following the Meiji Restoration, the government made surnames mandatory for all citizens in 1875 (Hisei Shinbutsu / Family Name Decree) to modernize taxation, conscription, and census tracking.
Nature & Geography: Because ordinary citizens had to scramble to pick or register a surname, many chose names derived from local geography, nature, or farming landscapes (Yamamoto meaning "base of the mountain", Sato). Japan now boasts hundreds of thousands of distinct surnames.
Philippines
Pre-Colonial Naming: Before Spanish colonization, Filipinos used indigenous naming systems (often single personal names or descriptive monikers), sometimes influenced by trade connections with China & Southeast Asian neighbors.
The Claveria Decree (1849): Spanish Governor-General Narciso Claveria issued a decree in 1849 requiring native families to select surnames from a vast Spanish-language catalog (Catálogo Alfabético de Apellidos) to improve tax collection & Catholic parish registries.
Modern Hybridity: As a result, Filipino surnames are predominantly Spanish (Dela Cruz, Santos), alongside indigenous and Chinese-derived surnames. Western naming order (first name, middle name/mother's maiden name, and last name) is standard.
Thailand
Mononym Tradition: For most of Siam's history, the general population used only a single given name (mononym), supplemented by nicknames, parental references, or hometowns.
The Surname Act of 1913: King Rama VI (Maha Vajiravudh), influenced by his education in Britain, introduced the Surname Act in 1913 to modernize state bureaucracy, census records, and military tracking.
Unique Uniqueness Rule: A unique feature of the 1913 law was that no two families could register the exact same surname. Because common words were quickly taken, families invented long, virtuous, or poetic compound words. Consequently, sharing a traditional Thai surname almost always implies a direct blood relation.
Indonesia
Absence of a Universal Surname Culture: Indonesia is a vast archipelago with over 300 ethnic groups, and most ethnic groups (such as the Javanese) traditionally do not use hereditary family surnames. Instead, many individuals go by a single given name (mononym, like Sukarno or Suharto) or multi-word personal names without a fixed family-name component.
Regional Exceptions: Certain ethnic groups do practice patrilineal or clan-based surnames, such as the Batak people in Sumatra (Sitorus, Nababan), Minangkabau matrilineal lineages, or Christian/Eastern Indonesian communities influenced by European or local clan traditions.
The Chinese-Indonesian Experience: During the Suharto regime (starting in the late 1960s), anti-Chinese assimilation policies forced ethnic Chinese Indonesians to drop traditional Chinese surnames & adopt Indonesian-sounding mononyms or names. After 1998, restrictions were lifted, though many families kept their adopted Indonesian names. Official Indonesian documents treat a person's entire name sequence as a single personal identifier rather than dividing it into first, middle, and last names
Turkey
Ottoman Era: Turks traditionally used given names followed by father's names, religious titles (such as Effendi or Pasha), or geographic/tribal tags rather than permanent European-style family names.
The 1934 Surname Law: Modern Turkey transformed its naming conventions when the Turkish Surname Law was enacted on June 21, 1934 (effective 1935), requiring every citizen to adopt a fixed, hereditary Turkish surname
Nigerian
Traditional Naming: Various ethnic groups (Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa, Fulani) historically relied on single given names, patronymics, clan lineages, or praise-names that reflected birthday circumstances or ancestral deities.
Colonial & Religious Shift: Fixed, hereditary Western and Islamic surnames became widespread during British colonial administration after the 1900s, Christian missionary schooling, and the deeper integration of Islam in northern regions.
Ghana
Origin & Structure: A distinctive feature of Ghanaian (particularly Akan) culture is the day-name system, where children are given a first name or surname based on the day of the week they were born, carrying deep symbolic meaning (e.g., Mensah for third-born children, or Cudjoe for a child born on Monday). Surnames also reflect ancestral clans, occupational trades, or spiritual beliefs (Quansah - "God is watching you").
Common Examples: Mensah, Nkrumah, Adu, Quansah.
Senegal
Origin & Structure: Senegalese surnames are deeply rooted in West African ethnic groups like the Wolof, Serer, and Fula/Pulaar. Many surnames trace back to ancient royal clans (such as Diop, a Wolof royal clan name), occupational castes, or Islamic lineage spread via trade and scholarship across the Sahel.
Ethiopia
Origin & Structure: Ethiopia traditionally does not use European-style hereditary family surnames. Instead, an individual’s second name is their father’s first name (patronymic), and sometimes followed by the grandfather’s first name. Names frequently carry Amharic or Ge'ez meanings tied to religious faith, gratitude, or virtues (Tadesse, Tesfaye - "hope").
Common Examples: Tadesse, Tesfaye
Kenya
Origin & Structure: Kenyan surnames vary by community (such as Kikuyu, Luo, or Kalenjin). Among the Kikuyu, names frequently honor ancestors or reflect cultural milestones (Mwangi). British colonization also introduced partial anglicization or record formalization, though traditional patronymic and clan-based naming structures remain culturally prominent.
Common Examples: Mwangi, Kenyatta, Otieno.
Morocco
Origin & Structure: Moroccan surnames are shaped by Amazigh (Berber) indigenous roots combined with centuries of Arab-Islamic history & Andalusian migration. Many surnames are patronymics (using Ibn meaning "son of"), tribal/geographic attributions (describing a region or city of origin), or honorific/royal lineage claims such as Alaoui (linked to the reigning Alaouite dynasty).
No, recognizing the historical origins of surnames does not sound like slavery. It is a factual description of how naming worked under the USA system during the Antebellum era & what happened afterwards.

What English or Western surnames Means
It refers to surnames of European linguistic origin English, Scottish, Irish, Welsh, German French, Dutch, etc. that became the norm in the USA and other Western societies. For Antebellum-Black / Anglo-Black / Anglo-Moor Americans in the USA the great majority of common surnames ( Washington, Williams, Johnson, Smith, James, Brown, Jackson & many others are of this type. As I documented earlier they are not automatically "slaveholders  names" though many are. After emancipation, Antebellum-Black Americans had the right to choose their own surnames, and the surnames they choose were for a variety of reasons. The process was more varied than the simple " everyone took the master's name" stereotype, but American, English, Western surnames became the standard or rule.
The Comparison to Other Groups
Globally, mononyms (single names) were historically the norm in most cultures. Aside from the Chinese, Europeans were among the first to adopt surnames during the Medieval period. However, between the 1500s & 1700s, surnames remained a privilege of the few, largely reserved for royalty, rulers, wealthy individuals, and landowners. The widespread adoption of family names by commoners, peasants, serfs, slave populations, and the landless occurred much later, often imposed by government decrees, for collecting taxes & tracking ownership of property.
Similarly, single given names were the standard across most traditional African cultures. Surnames were not widely adopted in Africa until the era of European colonialism in the 1900s. At that time, people began adopting family names derived from Islamic traditions, improvised terms, birthdates, religious rituals, occupations, environmental features, or descriptive phrases. Consequently, traditional African surnames as we understand them today did not exist prior to the 1900s. Individuals can honor and celebrate their broader African heritage while still deeply respecting the distinct lineage of their Antebellum-Black / Antebellum-Moor American ancestors, however taken on African or Islamic surnames is absolutely absurd, Islam is not a native African religion, it is Arabic, and it caused havoc across the African continent, isolating Western and Central Africa from non-Arabic middle-eastern and European cultures, the Arabs became middle-men between Europe, the middle-east, Asia and West Africa, in my opinion Africa would have been better-off practicing Coptic Christianity, a religion that was well establish in Africa by the Egyptians, Nubians, Libyans and Ethiopians in the 1st, 2nd & 3rd centuries, before they were invaded & conquered by the Arab-Muslim in the 7th & 8th century.

I lived worked and traveled through several African countries between 1994 - 1996, I nearly married a Cape-Malay Muslim girl in Cape Town. I wasn't impress with African culture, African food or Ancient African history. While regions like Egypt, Sudan, and Ethiopia possess extensively documented histories, physical artifacts, and ancient texts, finding non-Arabic written records, non-Arabic or pre-colonial physical artifacts, monuments, religious temples, architectural ruins, palaces and non-Islamic historical narratives on Western and Central Africa, specifically the Ghana, Mali, Songhai & Kanem-Bornu empires presented a considerable historical challenge.
Frederick Delk

text:
THE RECORD, DECLARED

IN THE ROYAL HOUSE OF GOOSE, October 31, 2026.
The Register Current of the Grievances of a Citizen of the United States of America

Every petition, inquiry, indictment, condemnation and damnation raised from this account, collected in one place, in the order raised, each beside its link. Each was declared in its own post, on its own sources, quoted from the documents themselves. Read them whole.

"A decent respect to the opinions of mankind requires that they should declare the causes." They have been declared, one by one. Here they are, together.

"To prove this, let Facts be submitted to a candid world."

WHERE IT BEGAN

WE THE PEOPLE · https://t.co/iPLyJ0zPEH
Against all 535 seated members of the 119th Congress
The first grievance, the one that opened the door. Six FY2026 bills, the defense authorization among them, charged section by section: reporting, notification, reprogramming and force-posture mandates that encroach on the President's powers under Article II. It asks the governors and attorneys general to seek Supreme Court review, and every State to investigate the financial backers of its delegation for foreign influence. Closed on Washington's Farewell Address.
https://t.co/JiqZZtMvOW

THE PETITION, THE INQUIRY AND THE INDICTMENTS

THE PETITION · to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Pope
A plea for the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness," raised in the Church's own law: in Latin, by a lay member of the faithful, under canon 212. To the Dicastery: a doctrinal Note declaring priests and prelates bound to put innocent human life before any temporal political end, and a declaration that their public, obstinate denial of the teaching John Paul II confirmed in Evangelium vitae 57 falls under penal law. To the Pope: a common effort with the Eastern Churches, in communion or not, to protect innocent children born and unborn; and a worldwide review of Church property accounts, so that no political influence bends the refuge the Church offers the needy.
https://t.co/UNnZwyrpQi

THE BANNER · A Citizen's Indictment and Condemnation
Against the ICC, the ICJ, the UN, the WTO, the EU, and the committees of Basel and Paris
The Constitution, the Uniform Code of Military Justice and the Declaration raised against every body that would bind Americans to law they never ratified. Six counts, each set against the clause it offends. Our rights are not granted by government; they are fenced off from it. Then the record of every time since 1919 the question was put and the Constitution answered it, even when our own Presidents were the ones asking.
https://t.co/NgTe8NVuBZ

BEFORE THE DAIS · An Inquiry
To the eight living Secretaries of State
Not a charge against any of them: a charge against what the office has been allowed to become. The standard Hamilton, Jay, Jefferson and the Foreign Service Act set for it, against what the government's own auditors found: fitness written as "should," training by accretion, posts left empty, authority on paper, and a revolving-door guard that lapses in 2027. Seven questions to all of them, and one to each on their own record. A paragraph each is enough.
https://t.co/pltubkVVeJ

IN CONGRESS ASSEMBLED · A Citizen's Indictment of the First Branch
Against the Senate and the House, under every majority that has held them
Nine counts: the purse let fall; war made without a declaration since 1942; the legislative power parcelled out to the agencies, the Federal Reserve and Basel; the legislative veto; the courts left unbuilt; a House grown to one member for every 761,169; judges in their own cause; the faction; and the enforcement clauses left asleep. The Declaration charged a King with power seized. These are charges of power abandoned: "He has abdicated Government here." Answer by the yeas and nays.
https://t.co/jAVsOSRHPl

ONE SUPREME COURT · A Citizen's Indictment of the Third Branch
Against the Court, and the Chief Justice who alone designates its secret benches
Ten counts on three duties. To check the branches: forty years of deference, a surveillance bench the watched cannot reach, the jury bargained away, courts it did not make, rights signed away in fine print. To judge between the States: sovereign States turned away from the only court they have. To guard the sovereignty: foreign custom let in by a second door, Missouri v. Holland, the Insular Cases, and the citizenship it would not decide. Answer by judgment, in a case.
https://t.co/vywTIPdChv

THE ROUNDS

ROUND I · THE EU · The Exits Already Written
Twenty U.S.–EU agreements the Executive may end on written notice, by their own terms, read out of the State Department's own Treaties in Force: passenger-name records, terrorist-finance tracking, Europol, Galileo–GPS and the air transport agreement among them. A nominal list of what can be done alone; the weighing is State's and Treasury's. The first of a round for every State, non-state actor and non-U.S. body that gets uppity with us.
https://t.co/smLQ4MK6jL

ROUND II · THE EBRD · The Door Already Written
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, charged in its own words; the way out, in its own charter. America paid for a bank to build open markets and private enterprise, and now stands behind one that pledges half its financing to green purposes, aligns every new investment to a treaty America left, takes its nature goals from a convention America never ratified, and names Brussels its largest green donor. The bill comes to Washington. The profit stays in London. The door: written notice, six months, no vote, no consent, and the money back to the Treasury.
https://t.co/gvoLSgGDS6

ROUND III · FRANCE · From the Present Time and Forever
A damnation of the French Republic, on France's own signature to the treaties of 1778. Fourteen counts, 1775 to 2019: help that came deniable and invoiced, an alliance that was a leash, our independence chained to a Spanish rock, our election worked from outside, our ships seized against its written promise, a throne raised on our border while the Union bled, a door opened to Japan, NATO shown the door. Convicted once already, by Act of Congress in 1798. On the French state, not the French people. Beneath it: what the Executive can end alone, and the dead paper still on the books.
https://t.co/WLkZcFFC8J

ROUND IV · BASEL · The Landlord
A damnation of the Bank for International Settlements and the committees under its roof: immunity "in time of peace and in time of war," and not one duty owed in return. Ten counts: founded over America's refusal, with America's banks; neutrality published while looted gold was banked; sentenced to liquidation at Bretton Woods and spared without a vote; the shield still at work this century; parent to the European Central Bank; and an offense against the Law of Nations, contrived to be neither sovereign nor subject. Its only American paper is a 1948 receipt for Nazi gold. The way out is a letter and an empty chair.
https://t.co/2NGjtqLGlN

ROUND V · THE PRESS · The Megaphone and the Muzzle
The mass dissemination machine, charged in one line: censorship, plus mass bullshit distribution. Eight counts against the owners, wires and platforms, and the fact-checkers paid or part-owned by them: two screens, one wallet, with foreign sovereign money in the equity; one script read in a hundred towns; headlines the documents never wrote; the public warned off its own research; politics pushed into the reprieve. The foreign hand, owned, influenced and funded, put on notice, Brussels the worst of it. None of the terms silences anyone. The plea: read the four pages, then the primary sources. They are free, and none of them has an opinion about you.
https://t.co/hJMoseJ9i4

ROUND VI · CANADA · Forever Free and Open
A condemnation of Canada, judged by its own Boundary Waters Treaty: navigation "forever … free and open." Twenty-five counts, 1777 to 2026: the road south for an invading army, raiders sheltered while the Union bled, fishermen seized, milk and quotas rigged, a law against bargaining with us, bourbon pulled from the shelves while Beijing's cars came in. Convicted already by GATT, the WTO, a USMCA panel and the President. On the Canadian state, not the Canadian people. Beneath it: 58 agreements the Executive can end alone, and a ledger that still lists NAFTA.
https://t.co/05lsCoaLYA

ROUND VII · THE CROWN · Unfeeling Brethren
A damnation of the United Kingdom, in the words Congress struck. In June 1776 Jefferson's draught turned on "our British brethren," and Congress cut its harshest lines lest they give offence. They are restored here: forts kept after the peace, envoys sent home for meddling, American opinion worked in secret, the bank we resolved to kill kept alive, the regimes' money run through our dollar, the enemy's oil insured, burdens handed to us and the ledger kept. A war debt unpaid since the 1930s, its bill run back at Britain's own rules. On the British state, and on the people who returned it to power. Britain only comes second because France exists. Beneath it: 141 exits, clause by clause.
https://t.co/B254o2kMkw

ROUND VIII · AUSTRALIA · The Gateway
Three tiers. A damnation of the government of Australia, judged by ANZUS against the memorandum that made Hobart Beijing's "gateway" to the ice: Darwin's port leased beside our Marines to a Chinese-owned company, a Commissioner who led Brussels and London on speech and tried to set what the whole world may see, Brussels' rules copied in. A condemnation of its failures: goods made by forced labour let in, a Chinese fleet firing live in the Tasman answered with a complaint about the notice, the Pacific lost to Beijing on its watch. And a hand extended to the Australian people, rough, real and as sick of their government's shit as we are of ours: go bilateral, peel off Beijing, lock down Oceania with us. Beneath it: 71 exits open now, clause by clause, 39 of them the Executive's alone.
https://t.co/X4dPDZNnPM

ROUND IX · NATO AND THE UNION · Such Subsidiary Bodies
A damnation of NATO as it stands in 2026, by its own fourteen articles, and of the European Union, for the abuse of American good faith, trust and sacrifice. An alliance that amended itself by communique, made war on a state that attacked no member while our House split 213 to 213, carried our forces past its own map, set middlemen between our forces and our purposes, let us carry about 62 percent of allied defence spending, and gave foreign courts the first claim on our soldiers. A Union that overruled its own peoples and planted its system in our hemisphere. Not against the nations of Europe, save France and England, damned already. To the twenty-seven, line by line: the clause each gave away, and the two doors, Articles 48 and 50. The terms stay within the lock Congress set, and not a piece beyond it.
https://t.co/OOPEwpRluu

ROUND X · THE UN AND DAVOS · Such Other Functions
A damnation of the United Nations, laid by its own Charter, and of the World Economic Forum beside it. A Human Rights Council that seats governments the UN's own investigators accused; a 2019 partnership between the Secretary-General and a Swiss foundation that no organ voted on; American money asked to "accelerate" a recommendation that binds no one; a Charter that opens "WE THE PEOPLES" and has come to treat them as human resources. The Forum: the heads of the European Central Bank, the IMF, the World Bank and the WTO, and BlackRock's chairman, seated as trustees of one Swiss foundation, and a stage where a sitting prime minister proposed ending anonymity on the platforms Americans speak on. Not against the Charter. Not against the nations under it.
https://t.co/iB27hON7lF

Read them whole, and read them with each other. Then read the four pages yourself: https://t.co/3U5xYhtlHs. They are yours, and no other people on earth holds the same ones.

TO THOSE WHO DO HOLD THE POWER
Every one but the petition is a grievance, raised in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances," and laid before the offices that hold the power I do not. I hold no office, and I set no terms. Terms with a foreign power are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry. The purse is the Congress's, consent to treaties is the Senate's, and judgment is the courts'. To each I defer. What touches national security is deferred, without contest, to those who hold it. Where a post sets terms, they are what I would do had I the power, not a demand of those who hold it. The remedies are lawful, and they are the People's: the ballot, Article V, and the petition.

The petition is the Holy See's to answer, and to it I defer: to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, and to the Holy Father, that he may act true to the faith he guards and for the good of all mankind. Peter was charged three times to feed the flock, and the lambs first.

We the People

IN CONGRESS, JULY 4, 1776

THE UNANIMOUS DECLARATION OF THE THIRTEEN UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,

WHEN IN THE COURSE OF HUMAN EVENTS, IT BECOMES NECESSARY FOR ONE PEOPLE TO DISSOLVE THE POLITICAL BANDS WHICH HAVE CONNECTED THEM WITH ANOTHER, AND TO ASSUME AMONG THE POWERS OF THE EARTH, THE SEPARATE AND EQUAL STATION TO WHICH THE LAWS OF NATURE AND OF NATURE'S GOD ENTITLE THEM, A DECENT RESPECT TO THE OPINIONS OF MANKIND REQUIRES THAT THEY SHOULD DECLARE THE CAUSES WHICH IMPEL THEM TO THE SEPARATION.

WE HOLD THESE TRUTHS TO BE SELF-EVIDENT, THAT ALL MEN ARE CREATED EQUAL, THAT THEY ARE ENDOWED BY THEIR CREATOR WITH CERTAIN UNALIENABLE RIGHTS, THAT AMONG THESE ARE LIFE, LIBERTY AND THE PURSUIT OF HAPPINESS.--THAT TO SECURE THESE RIGHTS, GOVERNMENTS ARE INSTITUTED AMONG MEN, DERIVING THEIR JUST POWERS FROM THE CONSENT OF THE GOVERNED, --THAT WHENEVER ANY FORM OF GOVERNMENT BECOMES DESTRUCTIVE OF THESE ENDS, IT IS THE RIGHT OF THE PEOPLE TO ALTER OR TO ABOLISH IT, AND TO INSTITUTE NEW GOVERNMENT, LAYING ITS FOUNDATION ON SUCH PRINCIPLES AND ORGANIZING ITS POWERS IN SUCH FORM, AS TO THEM SHALL SEEM MOST LIKELY TO EFFECT THEIR SAFETY AND HAPPINESS. PRUDENCE, INDEED, WILL DICTATE THAT GOVERNMENTS LONG ESTABLISHED SHOULD NOT BE CHANGED FOR LIGHT AND TRANSIENT CAUSES; AND ACCORDINGLY ALL EXPERIENCE HATH SHEWN, THAT MANKIND ARE MORE DISPOSED TO SUFFER, WHILE EVILS ARE SUFFERABLE, THAN TO RIGHT THEMSELVES BY ABOLISHING THE FORMS TO WHICH THEY ARE ACCUSTOMED. BUT WHEN A LONG TRAIN OF ABUSES AND USURPATIONS, PURSUING INVARIABLY THE SAME OBJECT EVINCES A DESIGN TO REDUCE THEM UNDER ABSOLUTE DESPOTISM, IT IS THEIR RIGHT, IT IS THEIR DUTY, TO THROW OFF SUCH GOVERNMENT, AND TO PROVIDE NEW GUARDS FOR THEIR FUTURE SECURITY.--SUCH HAS BEEN THE PATIENT SUFFERANCE OF THESE COLONIES; AND SUCH IS NOW THE NECESSITY WHICH CONSTRAINS THEM TO ALTER THEIR FORMER SYSTEMS OF GOVERNMENT. THE HISTORY OF THE PRESENT KING OF GREAT BRITAIN IS A HISTORY OF REPEATED INJURIES AND USURPATIONS, ALL HAVING IN DIRECT OBJECT THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ABSOLUTE TYRANNY OVER THESE STATES. TO PROVE THIS, LET FACTS BE SUBMITTED TO A CANDID WORLD.

HE HAS REFUSED HIS ASSENT TO LAWS, THE MOST WHOLESOME AND NECESSARY FOR THE PUBLIC GOOD.

HE HAS FORBIDDEN HIS GOVERNORS TO PASS LAWS OF IMMEDIATE AND PRESSING IMPORTANCE, UNLESS SUSPENDED IN THEIR OPERATION TILL HIS ASSENT SHOULD BE OBTAINED; AND WHEN SO SUSPENDED, HE HAS UTTERLY NEGLECTED TO ATTEND TO THEM.

HE HAS REFUSED TO PASS OTHER LAWS FOR THE ACCOMMODATION OF LARGE DISTRICTS OF PEOPLE, UNLESS THOSE PEOPLE WOULD RELINQUISH THE RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION IN THE LEGISLATURE, A RIGHT INESTIMABLE TO THEM AND FORMIDABLE TO TYRANTS ONLY.

HE HAS CALLED TOGETHER LEGISLATIVE BODIES AT PLACES UNUSUAL, UNCOMFORTABLE, AND DISTANT FROM THE DEPOSITORY OF THEIR PUBLIC RECORDS, FOR THE SOLE PURPOSE OF FATIGUING THEM INTO COMPLIANCE WITH HIS MEASURES.

HE HAS DISSOLVED REPRESENTATIVE HOUSES REPEATEDLY, FOR OPPOSING WITH MANLY FIRMNESS HIS INVASIONS ON THE RIGHTS OF THE PEOPLE.

HE HAS REFUSED FOR A LONG TIME, AFTER SUCH DISSOLUTIONS, TO CAUSE OTHERS TO BE ELECTED; WHEREBY THE LEGISLATIVE POWERS, INCAPABLE OF ANNIHILATION, HAVE RETURNED TO THE PEOPLE AT LARGE FOR THEIR EXERCISE; THE STATE REMAINING IN THE MEAN TIME EXPOSED TO ALL THE DANGERS OF INVASION FROM WITHOUT, AND CONVULSIONS WITHIN.

HE HAS ENDEAVOURED TO PREVENT THE POPULATION OF THESE STATES; FOR THAT PURPOSE OBSTRUCTING THE LAWS FOR NATURALIZATION OF FOREIGNERS; REFUSING TO PASS OTHERS TO ENCOURAGE THEIR MIGRATIONS HITHER, AND RAISING THE CONDITIONS OF NEW APPROPRIATIONS OF LANDS.

HE HAS OBSTRUCTED THE ADMINISTRATION OF JUSTICE, BY REFUSING HIS ASSENT TO LAWS FOR ESTABLISHING JUDICIARY POWERS.

HE HAS MADE JUDGES DEPENDENT ON HIS WILL ALONE, FOR THE TENURE OF THEIR OFFICES, AND THE AMOUNT AND PAYMENT OF THEIR SALARIES.

HE HAS ERECTED A MULTITUDE OF NEW OFFICES, AND SENT HITHER SWARMS OF OFFICERS TO HARRASS OUR PEOPLE, AND EAT OUT THEIR SUBSTANCE.

HE HAS KEPT AMONG US, IN TIMES OF PEACE, STANDING ARMIES WITHOUT THE CONSENT OF OUR LEGISLATURES.

HE HAS AFFECTED TO RENDER THE MILITARY INDEPENDENT OF AND SUPERIOR TO THE CIVIL POWER.

HE HAS COMBINED WITH OTHERS TO SUBJECT US TO A JURISDICTION FOREIGN TO OUR CONSTITUTION, AND UNACKNOWLEDGED BY OUR LAWS; GIVING HIS ASSENT TO THEIR ACTS OF PRETENDED LEGISLATION:

FOR QUARTERING LARGE BODIES OF ARMED TROOPS AMONG US:

FOR PROTECTING THEM, BY A MOCK TRIAL, FROM PUNISHMENT FOR ANY MURDERS WHICH THEY SHOULD COMMIT ON THE INHABITANTS OF THESE STATES:

FOR CUTTING OFF OUR TRADE WITH ALL PARTS OF THE WORLD:

FOR IMPOSING TAXES ON US WITHOUT OUR CONSENT:

FOR DEPRIVING US IN MANY CASES, OF THE BENEFITS OF TRIAL BY JURY:

FOR TRANSPORTING US BEYOND SEAS TO BE TRIED FOR PRETENDED OFFENCES:

FOR ABOLISHING THE FREE SYSTEM OF ENGLISH LAWS IN A NEIGHBOURING PROVINCE, ESTABLISHING THEREIN AN ARBITRARY GOVERNMENT, AND ENLARGING ITS BOUNDARIES SO AS TO RENDER IT AT ONCE AN EXAMPLE AND FIT INSTRUMENT FOR INTRODUCING THE SAME ABSOLUTE RULE INTO THESE COLONIES:

FOR TAKING AWAY OUR CHARTERS, ABOLISHING OUR MOST VALUABLE LAWS, AND ALTERING FUNDAMENTALLY THE FORMS OF OUR GOVERNMENTS:

FOR SUSPENDING OUR OWN LEGISLATURES, AND DECLARING THEMSELVES INVESTED WITH POWER TO LEGISLATE FOR US IN ALL CASES WHATSOEVER.

HE HAS ABDICATED GOVERNMENT HERE, BY DECLARING US OUT OF HIS PROTECTION AND WAGING WAR AGAINST US.

HE HAS PLUNDERED OUR SEAS, RAVAGED OUR COASTS, BURNT OUR TOWNS, AND DESTROYED THE LIVES OF OUR PEOPLE.

HE IS AT THIS TIME TRANSPORTING LARGE ARMIES OF FOREIGN MERCENARIES TO COMPLEAT THE WORKS OF DEATH, DESOLATION AND TYRANNY, ALREADY BEGUN WITH CIRCUMSTANCES OF CRUELTY & PERFIDY SCARCELY PARALLELED IN THE MOST BARBAROUS AGES, AND TOTALLY UNWORTHY THE HEAD OF A CIVILIZED NATION.

HE HAS CONSTRAINED OUR FELLOW CITIZENS TAKEN CAPTIVE ON THE HIGH SEAS TO BEAR ARMS AGAINST THEIR COUNTRY, TO BECOME THE EXECUTIONERS OF THEIR FRIENDS AND BRETHREN, OR TO FALL THEMSELVES BY THEIR HANDS.

HE HAS EXCITED DOMESTIC INSURRECTIONS AMONGST US, AND HAS ENDEAVOURED TO BRING ON THE INHABITANTS OF OUR FRONTIERS, THE MERCILESS INDIAN SAVAGES, WHOSE KNOWN RULE OF WARFARE, IS AN UNDISTINGUISHED DESTRUCTION OF ALL AGES, SEXES AND CONDITIONS.

IN EVERY STAGE OF THESE OPPRESSIONS WE HAVE PETITIONED FOR REDRESS IN THE MOST HUMBLE TERMS: OUR REPEATED PETITIONS HAVE BEEN ANSWERED ONLY BY REPEATED INJURY.

A PRINCE, WHOSE CHARACTER IS THUS MARKED BY EVERY ACT WHICH MAY DEFINE A TYRANT, IS UNFIT TO BE THE RULER OF A FREE PEOPLE.

NOR HAVE WE BEEN WANTING IN ATTENTIONS TO OUR BRITTISH BRETHREN. WE HAVE WARNED THEM FROM TIME TO TIME OF ATTEMPTS BY THEIR LEGISLATURE TO EXTEND AN UNWARRANTABLE JURISDICTION OVER US. WE HAVE REMINDED THEM OF THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF OUR EMIGRATION AND SETTLEMENT HERE. WE HAVE APPEALED TO THEIR NATIVE JUSTICE AND MAGNANIMITY, AND WE HAVE CONJURED THEM BY THE TIES OF OUR COMMON KINDRED TO DISAVOW THESE USURPATIONS, WHICH, WOULD INEVITABLY INTERRUPT OUR CONNECTIONS AND CORRESPONDENCE. THEY TOO HAVE BEEN DEAF TO THE VOICE OF JUSTICE AND OF CONSANGUINITY. WE MUST, THEREFORE, ACQUIESCE IN THE NECESSITY, WHICH DENOUNCES OUR SEPARATION, AND HOLD THEM, AS WE HOLD THE REST OF MANKIND, ENEMIES IN WAR, IN PEACE FRIENDS.

WE, THEREFORE, THE REPRESENTATIVES OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, IN GENERAL CONGRESS, ASSEMBLED, APPEALING TO THE SUPREME JUDGE OF THE WORLD FOR THE RECTITUDE OF OUR INTENTIONS, DO, IN THE NAME, AND BY AUTHORITY OF THE GOOD PEOPLE OF THESE COLONIES, SOLEMNLY PUBLISH AND DECLARE, THAT THESE UNITED COLONIES ARE, AND OF RIGHT OUGHT TO BE FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES; THAT THEY ARE ABSOLVED FROM ALL ALLEGIANCE TO THE BRITISH CROWN, AND THAT ALL POLITICAL CONNECTION BETWEEN THEM AND THE STATE OF GREAT BRITAIN, IS AND OUGHT TO BE TOTALLY DISSOLVED; AND THAT AS FREE AND INDEPENDENT STATES, THEY HAVE FULL POWER TO LEVY WAR, CONCLUDE PEACE, CONTRACT ALLIANCES, ESTABLISH COMMERCE, AND TO DO ALL OTHER ACTS AND THINGS WHICH INDEPENDENT STATES MAY OF RIGHT DO. AND FOR THE SUPPORT OF THIS DECLARATION, WITH A FIRM RELIANCE ON THE PROTECTION OF DIVINE PROVIDENCE, WE MUTUALLY PLEDGE TO EACH OTHER OUR LIVES, OUR FORTUNES AND OUR SACRED HONOR.

text:
ROUND X
SUCH OTHER FUNCTIONS
A CITIZEN'S DAMNATION OF THE UNITED NATIONS, BY ITS OWN CHARTER, AND OF THE WORLD ECONOMIC FORUM

Raised by a citizen of the United States under the Constitution and the Declaration of Independence, and laid before the President and the Congress in exercise of the right "to petition the Government for a redress of grievances"

AGAINST the United Nations as it stands in 2026: its Secretariat, its Human Rights Council, its subsidiary organs. AGAINST the World Economic Forum: its Foundation, its Board of Trustees, its stage at Davos.

Not against the Charter. This charge is laid by it. Not against the nations under it. Every one keeps its voice and its vote.

I. WHAT WE SIGNED

San Francisco, 26 June 1945. One hundred and eleven articles, opening "WE THE PEOPLES." It borrowed our Constitution's first words and gave the signature to "our respective Governments." Our Senate approved it 89 to 2.

It reaffirmed faith "in the dignity and worth of the human person." The Assembly "may make recommendations." Beyond its budget, only the Security Council binds. A private body gets "suitable arrangements for consultation," and nothing more. The Secretary-General performs "such other functions as are entrusted to him by these organs," and takes no "instructions from any government or from any other authority external to the Organization." Nothing in it authorizes the United Nations "to intervene in matters which are essentially within the domestic jurisdiction of any state."

The League we refused had a door: "Any Member of the League may, after two years' notice of its intention so to do, withdraw from the League," once its obligations were met. It left "regional understandings like the Monroe doctrine" standing. On 19 November 1919 our Senate rejected the treaty that carried it. The Charter has no written door and no Monroe. We ratified it anyway. We kept faith.

Eighty-one years, four amended articles. Article 23 still seats "the Republic of China" and "the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics." Everything else came by resolution and by signature.

Our law answers first. A plurality of our Supreme Court in 1957, and a majority in 1988: "no agreement with a foreign nation can confer power on the Congress, or on any other branch of Government, which is free from the restraints of the Constitution."

II. THE ORGANIZATION

It seats on its Human Rights Council the governments its own investigators accused. The Council was founded on "non-selectivity" and "the elimination of double standards and politicization." Its electors "shall take into account" a candidate's record. Its members "shall uphold the highest standards." In 2006 we were one of four votes against founding it, for exactly that: electors need only "take into account" a record.

China sits through 2026. Its own human rights office: detentions that "may constitute international crimes, in particular crimes against humanity."
Burundi sits through 2026. Its own inquiry: "crimes against humanity have been committed and continue to be committed."
Ethiopia sits through 2027. Its own news service, on its experts' final report: acts by the Ethiopian National Defence Forces, among others, "all of which constitute war crimes and crimes against humanity."

It can suspend by two thirds. It has, twice: Libya in 2011, Russia in 2022. It seated these three anyway. In 2023 it appointed Iran's ambassador to chair its Social Forum. Our mission was "appalled." In 2025 its Commission on the Status of Women was chaired by Saudi Arabia. We stopped taking part in the Council in February 2025.

It has partnered with a private foundation, and no organ voted on it. On 13 June 2019 the Secretary-General and the Forum's founder signed to "jointly accelerate the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development." The Charter's word is consultation. The Assembly's word was complement: partnerships "are a complement to, but are not intended as a substitute for, the commitment made by Governments." It set rules for partnerships. It never entrusted this one. Article 98 says entrusted. He signed jointly.

It has asked us to pay to accelerate a recommendation. The 2030 Agenda was adopted without a vote in 2015, our assent among the 193. A recommendation binds no one. In March 2025 our delegation answered: the Agenda and its goals "advance a program of soft global governance that is inconsistent with U.S. sovereignty and adverse to the rights and interests of Americans." The United States "rejects and denounces the 2030 Agenda" and "will no longer reaffirm them as a matter of course."

It bills us the most: 22 percent of its budget for 2025 to 2027. China, 20.

It has grown past its own articles. In January 2026 we began withdrawing from 66 organizations "Contrary to the Interests of the United States," 31 of them its own.

It has kept its dead. The enemy-state clauses stand, and so do the names of two states that no longer hold its seats.

Its Charter opens "WE THE PEOPLES." It has come to treat them as human resources: managed by recommendation, accelerated by partnership, judged by the accused.

III. THE FORUM

It was "founded in 1971 as a not-for-profit organization." Since 2015 it has been an "International Institution for Public-Private Cooperation" under Swiss law. Basel contrived by treaty to be neither sovereign nor subject. Davos took the title without the immunity: Bern guarantees its independence and freedom of action, exempts it from federal tax, and lets it move gold at will. In 2020 Bern signed on to use it "more effectively as a strategic platform."

Its trustees: the President of the European Central Bank; the Managing Director of the IMF; the President of the World Bank Group; the Director-General of the WTO, a body beside the Charter, not of it; a sitting head of state; and, listed first as the Forum's own co-chair, the chairman of BlackRock. Europe's money, the world's lending and the world's trade rules, kept as trustees of a Swiss foundation.

On 24 August 2016 it elected Germany's Defense Minister, Ursula von der Leyen, a trustee. Three years later she led the European Commission. On 16 January 2024 she stood on its stage. Its risk report "makes for a stunning and sobering read." For business, the top concern "is not conflict or climate." "The starting point for that is to look deeper at the Global Risk Report." Of her Digital Services Act: "we defined the responsibilities of large internet platforms on the content they promote and propagate." In July 2025 four sitting Commissioners took co-chairs of its pillars. Its report was her starting point. The Union's law, already written, was her answer.

From its stage, and from its own:

Spain's Prime Minister, Davos, January 2025: "I propose putting an end to anonymity on social media." "One social media user, one real ID," every account linked "to an European Digital Identity Wallet," users unmasked "in the case of a crime," CEOs "held personally accountable." These are the platforms Americans speak on. Our Supreme Court has protected anonymous speech since 1960.

Australia's eSafety Commissioner, a Forum author, in her court filing of 22 April 2024: X could "remove the material entirely from the X service," and "Merely geo-blocking the material in Australia is not enough." One nation's regulator asked an American platform to erase a video for the whole world. She dropped the case in June.

Not every trustee, member or speaker said these things. These did, in their own words.

IV. WHAT WE GAVE

Its first members included the signers of "the Declaration by United Nations of 1 January 1942." Its ratifications came to our Government. Its text lies "in the archives of the Government of the United States of America." Its house stands in New York. It bills us more than any nation on earth. What we give, we can withhold. In 2025 we withheld the Human Rights Council's share. In 2026 we began leaving sixty-six bodies.

We founded it. Every Member keeps its voice and its vote. Let the votes be cast and the vetoes used as the Charter wrote them, not "as a matter of course." A United Nations held to the Charter that seats its five permanent members is the only one that can host real dialogue again.

For seating the accused to judge the rest; for joining its Secretary-General's name to a foundation's agenda without a vote; for asking our money to accelerate what binds no one; for keeping its dead and calling it order: the United Nations of 2026 stands damned by its own Charter. The Forum stands damned beside it.

THE TERMS I WOULD SET
I hold no office and set no terms. Terms with the United Nations are the President's to set and the Department of State's to carry, and to both I defer. The purse is the Congress's. These would be the terms: the Charter's core restored, its founder its first beneficiary, the withdrawals standing.
I. The door. The League's: two years' notice, obligations met.
II. The review. In 1955 the Assembly, with our vote, decided a conference to review the Charter "shall be held at an appropriate time." Move for it. A review is not a withdrawal.
III. The veto stays. Every vote cast, every veto used. Nothing "as a matter of course."
IV. The partnership ends. Article 71 is the only door, Article 98 the only warrant. Until it ends, our share of any cost it carries is withheld.
V. The Human Rights Council. No American seat and no American dollar until its own standard binds.
VI. The purse. Our share never rises. Twenty-two percent buys a Charter, not an agenda.
VII. The withdrawals stand until each body answers to its own charter. The United Nations' own house is the Senate's and the Congress's: the Charter, the Headquarters Agreement, the immunities convention. Its agencies carry their own doors; where one had none, our law wrote it. UNESCO's closes for us on December 31.
VIII. Article 2(7) is honored.
IX. The dead text is struck.
X. No partnership. An American official may speak in Davos as anyone may. None signs for the United States with the Forum, sits on its boards, or co-chairs its work. No federal grant, partnership or contract goes to the Forum itself.
XI. Conduct, not membership. No federal contract, grant or partnership with any body, at home or abroad, that carries a foreign authority's rules onto any right our Constitution secures to our citizens, our nationals, and every person within our jurisdiction. Association is protected. Conduct is not.
XII. No reach. Nothing made under the United Nations' name touches a right our Constitution secures. A treaty cannot do it. A signature cannot either.
XIII. No reaffirmation, no payment. We stopped reaffirming the 2030 Agenda. Stop paying to "accelerate" it.

Basel. The EBRD. You were charged in Rounds IV and II. You are on notice.

To Davos: you were a conference. You made yourself a counterpart. You have been named.

To the Secretariat: read Article 98. Then read Article 100.

The tenth. Read it with all that came before: the petition to the Holy See, for the unalienable rights of all peoples, "Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness"; the inquiry before the Secretaries of State; the indictments of the Congress and of the Supreme Court; the damnation of the International Criminal Court; and nine rounds: the Union, the EBRD, France, Basel, the press, Canada, the Crown, Australia, NATO.

We the People

P.S. A heads-up for the Department of State, while you're at it. Your own Treaties in Force, as of January 1, 2026, still lists the Declaration by United Nations, signed at Washington on January 1, 1942. In it, each government "pledges itself to employ its full resources, military or economic, against those members of the Tripartite Pact and its adherents with which such government is at war." Its parties still include the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia. China's footnote reads "Pre-1949 agreement, applicable only to Taiwan." It is an executive agreement. No Senate required. Yours to handle.

text:
THE ABUNDANCE OF EXISTENCE. 

Whenever life overwhelms me, I cry. I acknowledge my emotions, confront my circumstances, then somewhere between surrender and acceptance, I redirect my awareness towards abundance.

The immeasurable richness of existence itself. 

I return to nature, meditation, to the universe, to the quiet understanding that there is something profoundly beautiful about being alive that humanity has almost forgotten how to appreciate.

We spend our lives governed by the architecture of human civilisation. 

Time dictates our movements, responsibilities consume our energy, and expectations accumulate until living begins to resemble an endless obligation to survive.

We awaken to schedules, surrender our hours to necessity, measure our progress against expectations and retire each evening knowing tomorrow will demand much of the same.

Somewhere within this perpetual cycle, the extraordinary privilege of existence becomes overshadowed by the exhaustion of maintaining it.

What a strange contradiction.

We inhabit a universe of incomprehensible magnificence.

An entire universe existing in extraordinary harmony, long before humanity decided that the value of life should be measured by productivity, possessions and time.

This 3D existence can be exhausting.

Yet beneath the physical, I believe there is something infinitely greater.

Energy = Consciousness. 

The extraordinary abundance of existence itself.

The same universe that gave birth to the stars gave birth to us.

We are not separate from nature. 

We are an expression of it.

Oceans move with the gravitational embrace of the moon. Birds navigate the heavens without calendars or clocks. Ancient trees draw nourishment from intricate networks beneath the earth.

Nature does not measure its significance through achievement.

Its beauty exists without validation or justification.

We, too, belong to this extraordinary expression of existence.

Yet our physical vessels grow weary.

Our nervous systems absorb prolonged stress, our bodies surrender to fatigue, and our minds become overwhelmed by a world that rarely accommodates stillness.

Sometimes being human feels less like living and more like enduring.

But consciousness offers us something extraordinary.. the capacity to recognise suffering without allowing it to define the entirety of our existence.

Through us, matter has become capable of wonder. 

Through our awareness, the universe can contemplate itself.

And this is where my understanding of abundance begins.

I can be exhausted yet appreciate sunlight against my skin. I can carry sorrow while remaining profoundly grateful for the privilege of experiencing life.

There is no contradiction in suffering and gratitude occupying the same heart.

We have become so accustomed to attaching happiness to external circumstances that we postpone peace until life meets some imaginary standard of perfection.

Yet existence does not wait for favourable circumstances before revealing its beauty.

I can return to nature, feel the earth beneath my feet and remember I belong to something infinitely greater than the difficulties occupying my mind.

Nothing around me has necessarily changed.

But something within me has.

Abundance is not an escape from reality. 

It is a deeper appreciation of existence.

Happiness was never meant to be the reward for finally getting life right, but something available when we remember the extraordinary privilege of being alive.

When I return my consciousness to the abundance of WHAT WE ARE, rather than WHO WE ARE, I remember that my circumstances are something I am experiencing, not the entirety of my existence.

And suddenly, life feels lighter.

I AM NOT DENYING THE WEIGHT OF MY HUMAN EXPERIENCE. 

I AM REMEMBERING THE MAGNIFICENCE OF MY EXISTENCE. 🙏🤍💋

Hegseth offers full-throated endorsement of Trump’s arch amid legal battle 

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told a federal judge that President Donald Trump’s proposed triumphal arch is a “generational national defense opportunity” in a legal briefing arguing the project is vital to protecting the nation’s capital. 

Originally proposed as a monument to celebrate the country’s 250th birthday, Trump last month debuted a new justification for building it, saying it would double as a tourist attraction and military complex where drones and ammunition could be stored and military snipers could be posted. 

The surprise proposal for this additional use of the 250-foot arch came as the project – a personal endeavor of the President that has become a key part of his Trump area  and his recent Executive Order  (Making Federal Architecture Beautiful Again) and to support his legacy  which faces a slew of criticism and two lawsuits aimed at stopping its construction. 

In a written declaration submitted Wednesday, Hegseth defended Trump’s new rationale for the planned structure at Memorial Circle, a busy traffic circle between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

Tear your eyes away from the Trumps triumphal arch for a moment and consider the . new Tennessee Federal courthouse that is the real face of the President Trump-era future architectural legacy.

Just this last week in Tennessee, more than 500 miles away from Washington, DC, officials quietly unveiled a far more revealing illustration of the US President Trumps future architectural legacy.

Set to open in 2030, Chattanooga’s new courthouse will be a muscular Art Deco Greek temple. More than an imposing expression of judicial power, this state building also symbolizes something of national significance: It’s the first major new design announced by America’s federal building agency since Trump’s executive order, “Making Federal Architecture Beautiful Again.” Its beauty is therefore now a matter of both architectural and political debate.

Almost a year has passed since President Trump formalized his disdain for modernism, postmodernism and brutalism by mandating that major federal buildings be designed in “classical and traditional” styles.

One further suggested way to celebrate President Trump’s magnificent presidency and his demonstrate his achievements to the American public, as well as delivering a significant gift to the America people would be to re-develop Camp David into a truly beautiful Abbey where President Trump and future Presidents can host visiting Kings and Queens and other Presidents when they visit the United States.

Many past presidents have proposed such developments at Camp David, but no one has succeeded to follow through and deliver such a wonderful facility.

Thus, a possible development by President Trump, to be considered as a further major legacy to the US people and future presidents, is the construction of a great architectural legacy (under his “Making Federal Architecture Beautiful Again”) in President Trump’s name, similar to the White House complex ballroom and the Grand Trump Arch de Trump, celebrating the 250th year of the Great American Experiment

Camp David is a 125-acre (51-hectare) country retreat for the President of the United States. It lies in the wooded hills of Catocin Mountain Park In Frederik County, Maryland near the towns of Thurmont and Emmitsburg about 62 miles north-northwest of the national capital city, Washington DC.

However, what is really needed is a grand opulent castle or abbey that can accommodate and entertain very important visitors, visiting royalty and Presidents from across the world. Also, whilst it has a tiny golf course (one green and 4 Tees), plus a driving range, what it lacks is a tremendous golf course, fit for a President and his visitors plus an opulent Helipad

Thus as part of President Trump’s legacy, he should transform Camp David into something like the grand mansion of Downton Abbey in the United Kingdom, with the plan to re-name Camp David as Trump Abbey or Trump Castle.

The aim of this further Trump legacy would be to completely rebuild a magnificent  and opulent manor house or castle to replace the current rather dreary Camp David.

Downtown Abbey is of course based upon the Highclere Castle near Newbury in Hampshire, England .

Highclere Castle  (Downton Abbey) is a Grade 1 listed grand country house (or castle) built in 1679 and largely renovated during the 1840s, with a park designed by Capability Brown in the 18th century. The 5,000-acre (2,000-hectare) estate  in Highclere about five miles (eight kilometres) south of Newbury Berkshire, in England and 9+1⁄2 miles (15 kilometres) north of Andover in Hampshire.

The 19th-century renovation is in a Jacobean and Italianate style produced by architect Charles Barry. It is the country seat of the Hereditary British Earls of Carnarvon a branch of the Anglo-Welsh Herbert family

Going back to the Trump triumphal arch, the Secretary of War said that the location of the triumphal arch overlooks a number major national sites that are frequented by federal officials and its height will create elevation advantage and line-of-sight connectivity, while its central location will improve the ability to identify and assess potential threats, Hegseth argued. 

“It will be utilized as a dual-purpose structure: a major national monument that also incorporates military utility to support Homeland defense,” he said. “The elevated position can also support authorized protective-overwatch and counter-sniper personnel by improving observational, situational awareness and coordination with other security elements.” 

In addition to Hegseth, Secretary of Homeland Security, Markwayne Mullin, also defended the need for the arch’s dual purpose, saying the location “provides opportunities for increased capability for information -sharing and logistical coordination.” 

The full-throated endorsements for the arch’s potential national security uses from two cabinet members comes as the project is facing key tests to its progress. 

Hegseth’s and Mullin’s statements were part of the government’s submissions in a lawsuit being heard in the US District Court for the District of Columbia aimed at stopping the arch’s construction.

And next Thursday, the arch will be reviewed by the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC), the last of two federal agencies overseeing architectural and design changes in Washington, D.C. that must approve the project. 
If approved by NCPC, the administration has already said they will start construction as early as that same day. 

However, final plans for the arch submitted to the NCPC for its November 5th meeting that were released last week included no mention of the military component. 
The plans excluded features such as the drones and snipers that Trump described in September, and the contours of the arch in the plans did not appear to reflect a national security purpose. Instead, they describe the project as a “ceremonial gateway” to the nation’s capital. 

Hegseth’s Wednesday filing stated that the military components would not require any structural modifications or alterations. “The security features will be fully integrated into the existing design,” he wrote. 

Trump has also claimed the need for national security enhancements as the primary justification for his project to build a White House ballroom where the East Wing once stood.

A triumphal arch doubling as a security and military facility would be an extraordinary departure from the original concept. 

The proposed 161-foot observation deck would also turn it into a major tourist attraction. And the idea of transforming Camp David into a grand presidential estate would be an equally dramatic architectural undertaking. Whether these visions become reality, they would leave a very visible and long-lasting mark on Washington and the Trump presidency.

Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

text:
HIS VOICE. 🎤

Music became his escape from a world that had treated him so cruelly.

I could hear the hurt in every word he sang.

And I could see something else.

A man who had been knocked down over and over but refused to stop singing.

I wanted to help him.

I offered him some money, food, clean clothes, and an opportunity to record music.

I told him I believed in his talent.

And I wanted him to know that somebody out there cared.

That encounter inspired me to write and produce a song called:

🎵 “TAKE ME AWAY — TO WHERE THE GOOD TIMES ROLL.”

It’s a song about wanting to escape the pain of yesterday.

About leaving behind the darkness.

About dreaming of a better tomorrow.

About wanting to go somewhere where the good times roll and the memories don’t hurt anymore.

I didn’t write this song to become famous.

I wrote it because I wanted to give a struggling street artist something that could never be taken away from him.

A SONG THAT TELLS HIS STORY.

When you listen to this song, remember something.

That homeless person sitting on the sidewalk might have a talent the whole world deserves to hear.

He might have been somebody’s little boy who just needed love.

He might have survived things you couldn’t imagine.

And sometimes all it takes is one person to stop, listen, and say:

“BROTHER, I BELIEVE IN YOU.” ❤️

That’s why I do what I do.

From Waterbury, Connecticut, to Florida, to Malibu and Venice Beach, California, I’ve met people from every walk of life.

And I’ve learned one thing.

EVERYBODY HAS A STORY.

Sometimes that story becomes a song. 🎵

And sometimes that song gives somebody hope.

God bless every struggling musician, every homeless soul, and everyone fighting battles the world knows nothing about. 🙏❤️

NEVER JUDGE SOMEONE BY WHERE THEY SLEEP. JUDGE THEM BY WHAT’S IN THEIR HEART.

Much love,
TANGO BRONSON ❤️

Nipton, CA – Minor injuries were reported in a traffic collision involving a big rig that happened Thursday morning in Nipton, the California Highway Patrol reported.

The incident transpired around 6:33 a.m. on October 29, 2026, on the northbound 15 Freeway, just half a mile north of Yates Well Road.

A gray Honda CRV and a white big rig were involved in the accident. The Honda went about 40 feet off the roadway into a ditch, and the semi-truck pulled over to the shoulder.

The Honda was occupied by four people, including a child of approximately 5 years. A male occupant of the car said he was bleeding on his left arm near the elbow. The juvenile experienced signs of vomiting.

Firefighters and paramedics responded to the scene and offered medical aid to the victims.

The Honda was towed away from the scene.

text:
❯ Demoscene: Shapeshift by Cocoon
Two days before Revision 2016 the soundtrack changed, and the new one ran two minutes longer. The demo was finished at the party, and it won the PC demo competition by 145 points.
⠀
Watch it: https://t.co/tjm4Q4b1OA
⠀
On Easter Sunday, 27 March 2016, twenty entries ran in the PC demo compo at Revision in Saarbrücken. "Revision went off when this came on," one visitor wrote on Pouët that night, and added, "Hard earned win!" The count gave Shapeshift by Cocoon 1,298 points, with instant god by cncd and Fairlight second on 1,153.
⠀
■ FOUR NAMES AND A FRENCH GROUP
⠀
Cocoon are an all-French PC demo group, formed in 1997, whose catalogue reaches from MS-DOS demos of the nineties to recent work on the Amiga and the Atari ST. The nfo of Shapeshift credits GUILLE for the codework and NTSC for visuals and direction, with TINEIDAE on the soundtrack and, according to Pouët, Rork on graphics. It asks for a fast DX11 card on 64-bit Windows, with sound through FMOD.
⠀
■ NO LIMIT BUT THE CLOCK
⠀
A PC demo carries no size limit, and the final ships a data file of 140,192,083 bytes. Plenty of the scene's finest work lives within 4,096 bytes or on a single floppy; this one had the opposite freedom, and its limit came from the calendar.
⠀
ntsc told the story on Pouët that evening. The soundtrack had to change two days before the party, and the new music ran two minutes longer, in a rather different style. With only the intro and the city scene in the timeline on arrival, six minutes were finished in the hall. The skull part, in ntsc's words, "was done in less 20 mn from scratch". Another scener replied that people watching could not imagine how much work had gone in during the party.
⠀
The new music is Shapeshift by Tineidae, from the album Shadows, released on Tympanik Audio in December 2014. Demo and track share the name, and the visuals were cut in a hurry to a piece of music that had been out for some sixteen months.
⠀
■ A CITY WITH A TYRELL SIGN
⠀
The comments keep returning to the city. HellMood wrote that "the 'chinatown' scene alone deserves a game spin off", and cce simply: "The Neo Tokyo cityscape made me weep." When someone spotted the Blade Runner borrowing, ntsc was plainly delighted and pointed to a Tyrell logo in the background, the sort of thing one finds on the third viewing, mind.
⠀
The rest of the demo turns to abstract shapes, and there too the comments dwell on the light. cupe called Cocoon's tech "probably the most mature in the scene", and Zavie, after the final, singled out the global illumination: "the possibilities offered by your GI are really cool."
⠀
■ REVISION 2016
⠀
01 Shapeshift, Cocoon: 1,298
02 instant god, cncd & fairlight: 1,153
03 Through the Cracks, Still: 976
04 True Colors, Still: 955
05 The Zarahustler, Jugz: 907
⠀
Pouët counts 107 thumbs up against a single one down, which says a fair bit about the hall. The team had worked on Titan cards with no time to test others, so a final followed: its executable is dated 27 November 2016, and Zavie wrote that "the final clearly improves over the party version". The note under the video lists a GTX 1080 and a laptop GTX 960M, the latter "slow but it run".
⠀
A demo without a limit on its size found one on the clock, and still finished first.
⠀

text:
🎸 WHAT A BEAUTIFUL RIDE

A New Blues Album by P.T. Lucas

One man. One guitar. One microphone. A whole lot of heart.

What a Beautiful Ride is a journey back to the roots of American blues, inspired by the raw, soulful sounds of the 1930s Mississippi Delta and legendary bluesmen like Robert Johnson and Howlin’ Wolf.

But these aren’t songs about giving up. They’re songs about waking up, letting go, finding joy, and remembering what really matters.

In a world overwhelmed by politics, division, judgment, endless opinions, and 24-hour bad news, this album asks a simple question:

Whatever happened to just enjoying being alive?

Remember when we spent more time laughing together than arguing? When a good conversation, a little music, a night with friends, or simply watching the sunset was enough?

That’s what this album is about.

Songs like Turn Off the Noise, Let Them Think, World Peace Brother, A Little Heaven Here Today, and What a Beautiful Ride remind us that life has so much more to offer than arguments, resentment, and the endless pursuit of things that don’t really matter.

It’s about turning off the noise, letting people think what they want, choosing kindness over being right, and realizing that happiness isn’t something we have to keep chasing.

Sometimes a little heaven is already right here today.

These songs celebrate faith, forgiveness, individuality, gratitude, world peace, and the simple beauty of everyday life.

Sometimes they’re funny. Sometimes they’re a little sarcastic. Sometimes they’re deeply personal. But every song carries the same message:

Life is too short to spend it angry, divided, or worried about what everybody else thinks.

Musically, we stripped everything down to its roots. No big production. No elaborate orchestration. Just the spirit of an old bluesman sitting alone in a room, playing his guitar and telling the truth as he sees it.

Love somebody. Forgive somebody. Laugh a little louder. Stop trying to impress everybody. Turn off the television. Put down the arguments. Pick up a guitar. Spend time with the people you love.

And above all, remember to thank God for another day.

I’ve been through enough in this life to know that tomorrow isn’t promised. But I’ve also learned that every day we’re given is another opportunity to love, create, laugh, and make something beautiful.

I don’t know what tomorrow holds, and I don’t need to.

I’m still here. I’m still dreaming. I’m still making music.

And what a beautiful ride it’s been. ❤️

— P.T. Lucas

Persistence gets it. Consistency keeps it. Gratitude grows it.
