text:
The Girl Who Was Left Behind (Halloween Monster Roleplay 6) Part 30
The sound of skeletons cheering fills the room.
Well, mostly it's just hissing, rattling, and a great deal of jaw-clattering, since these fellows can't actually talk, but their hearts are in the right place. It's a touching display of loyalty, really, although I must admit that standing among hundreds of skeletons makes me feel a little underdressed.
And if there's one thing I cannot stand, it's blending in.
“I need a cloak! Black as midnight! Go find me an outfit!”
Peter immediately points in several directions, and the skeletons scatter, rummaging through ancient chests, broken coffins, and whatever unfortunate storage spaces this dungeon has accumulated over the centuries. Somewhere in the darkness, a skeleton knocks over a shelf, another begins hissing in what I assume is an argument, and a third emerges carrying a single boot.
I don't need a boot.
Eventually, they return with a rotten black cloak, some armor that is ornate, impractical, and absolutely magnificent, and a scepter with a skull mounted on top. Its empty eye sockets glow red, as red as the eyes of every skull I have ever seen, although these seem to burn with a little more purpose.
I take it in my hand. It feels strangely familiar.
Not like a weapon, exactly. More like something I once held while a thousand people knelt before me.
I shake off the thought. No time for that.
The army rallies around me, lifting me onto a stone platform so I can overlook my loyal subjects. The cloak drapes over my shoulders, and the old armor rattles against my ribs. I raise my scepter.
“Listen up, my magnificent collection of walking inconveniences!”
The hissing dies down.
“You have waited hundreds of years for your Queen to return. You served her in life, and you have continued to serve her in death. Now it is time for that loyalty to be requited! We are going to fix history! We are going to stop this palace from changing anyone else, and we are going to storm the sanctuary to put an end to the Father's wicked ways!”
The skeletons raise their weapons.
“Then, at long last, we shall have peace! The one thing every soldier, living or dead, ought to strive for! So tell me, my friends, who is ready to change history?”
The chamber erupts into a tremendous hiss, an awful, joyous roar that makes the ancient dust shake loose from the ceiling.
I feel the Spirit of Halloween stir in my ribs. For a moment, I almost feel like a queen again. Then Peter taps me on the shoulder. I look down. He points toward the wall.
Tap.
Tap.
Tap.
Oh, for the love of..
The sound is coming from the other side of the stones, slow and deliberate, as if somebody is knocking on the door of a house they haven't visited in a very long time.
“Don't be such a baby,” I tell him. “It's probably pipes blowing air or something.”
A metallic groan answers me. Then a rusted hand punches through the wall. The fingers spread, grasping at empty air. A second hand appears beside it. The stone around them cracks.
“Or,” I add, “it's the perfect reason for us to get the hell out of here.”
The skeletons begin backing away, weapons raised, their confidence evaporating rather quickly.
I snatch up my map. Or rather, the map I made. The scribblings have changed. The passageways twist in different directions, several routes have disappeared, and the little markings I made to remember our path have rearranged themselves into something resembling a child's drawing of a particularly angry spider.
The journal is worse. The old maps have vanished completely. Only one sentence remains on the page, written in dark, uneven letters.
THE FIRST COMMAND WAS NEVER GIVEN BY THE BOY.
I stare at it. Then I look at the hand still clawing through the wall.
“Right. Very informative. Thank you, mysterious book.”
The hand closes around a loose stone. 
Crack.
I jump down from my platform, my armor clanking, and point toward a narrow passage marked on my map.
“There! Our way out! Let me lead the charge!”
I pause.
“And make sure it's actually real.”
With the help of several soldiers, I pry up a heavy slab of stone, revealing a passageway beneath it. The opening is barely wide enough for me, and I have the distinct impression that this particular tunnel was designed for people who had never eaten a meal in their lives.
Fortunately, being mostly bones has its advantages.
The passage is dark and damp, black as sin, with a sour smell of wet earth, ancient dust, and something faintly metallic. Our torch throws trembling shadows across the walls, revealing little carvings that look almost like faces when the light passes over them.
We proceed single file.
The tunnels twist and bend, leading us through passages that seem to grow narrower with every turn. In several places, the ceiling dips so low that even my skull nearly scrapes against it.
I consult my map.
Left.
Then right.
Then left again.
At some point, left becomes right, and the floor begins sloping upward when I distinctly remember it sloping downward.
“Oh, great,” I mutter, examining the wretched paper. “Even my own drawings are trying to kill me.”
Peter leans over my shoulder.
“Stop looking at it,” I tell him. “You're not helping.”
The ink shifts. A new symbol appears. It is a circle divided by a vertical line, with two letters carved inside.
Q.
Y.
I stop. Peter bumps into me, and the skeleton behind him bumps into Peter, producing a chain reaction of clattering bones and very undignified hissing.
“What's this?” I ask.
Peter points at the symbol. Then he begins nodding. A lot.
“You've seen this before?”
More nodding.
“Where?”
Peter taps his own chest, then gestures toward the army. I look again.
Queen Yvaine.
The Queen's personal seal. I remember seeing the symbol before, on the scattered relics and faded records of this miserable place. It belongs to the queen these soldiers once served My queen, apparently. I look at Peter.
“You remember her?”
He pauses. Then he slowly nods. I almost ask him what she was like. But something in the way he holds his skull makes me reconsider. The poor fellow looks as though he's trying to remember a face that's been rubbed away from a painting.
Instead, I ask, “What's up ahead?”
Peter shrugs. All he knows is that the room ahead is important.
We proceed cautiously, following the map until the tunnel opens into a large chamber. And immediately, I know something is wrong. The room is mostly empty. There are scattered bones across the floor, a few broken weapons, and a layer of dust so thick that our footprints stand out like fresh wounds. The walls are covered with old carvings, most of them worn away by time.
In the center of the room is a circular depression in the stone. I step across it. The moment my foot touches the far side, every skeleton behind me begins hissing. Not their usual cheerful hiss. This is a warning. I turn around.
“What?”
They stand at the threshold, refusing to move. Their empty sockets are fixed on the floor beneath my feet.
“Look, I'm sorry if you knew these guys,” I tell them, glancing at the scattered bones. “We'll come back for them later. But Halloween is almost here, and we have a ritual to interrupt.”
They don't move. Peter takes a step forward, then stops. His skull tilts toward the center of the chamber. I follow his gaze. There, beneath the dust, is the Queen's seal. The same Q and Y. A faint magical aura pulses around it, so weak that my echoes can barely make sense of it. I can see traces of old enchantments, overlapping in layers, each one wrapped around the next.
Not a simple ward. Something much older. Something holding. Then the walls giggle.
“Oh, my. So close, yet so far. What a silly little skeleton man. Or are you a boy?”
I clench my jaw.
“It's whatever you want. I don't care. What is going on?”
“You think I know everything?”
“You act like it.”
“Hmmm. Perhaps.”
Her voice drifts through the chamber, sometimes from the ceiling, sometimes from beneath the floor, sometimes from the very stones around my feet.
“The gem told me a little something about your cute little army.”
I glance at the journal.
“What did it tell you?”
“Oh, I wouldn't want to spoil the surprise.”
“I don't have time for games.”
“Then perhaps you should think about why anyone would leave an entire army in a dungeon for hundreds of years.”
I look at the soldiers.
“Why did the Queen never come back?” the Girl asks. “Or did she choose not to come back?” I turn toward the seal. The bones scattered across the floor suddenly seem much less random. Their positions form a pattern.
The remains are arranged around the circular depression, some placed deliberately, others embedded into the stone itself. The old weapons are not strewn about after a battle. They are positioned like markers. My magical echoes flicker. For a heartbeat, I see the room as it once was. Skeletons kneeling around the circle. A figure standing in the middle.
The Queen.
And behind her, something enormous, something that makes the walls seem to bend away from it. Then the vision vanishes.
“They're guarding something,” I whisper.
“Oh, very good!”
The Girl's delighted voice makes my bones itch.
“They're keeping something in. Something old and powerful. That's why the Queen left. That's why she never came back.”
I stare at the seal. The skeletons behind me have gone completely still.
“What's beyond the door?”
“Go on. Find out.”
“What am I supposed to do? Break the seal?”
“That's easy. Just leave.”
The wall gives a soft, amused chuckle.
“Or leave them behind, and they can return to their proper places. They can be the protectors they were meant to be. Be selfless for a change.”
I look at Peter. He is standing rigidly, his weapon lowered, his skull turned toward the seal. I can almost feel the conflict in him. Duty. Loyalty. An order that has survived centuries, perhaps longer than his memories.
“Like you?” I ask the Girl.
“Like me indeed.”
For a moment, the chamber is quiet. I should stop. I know I should. The army's original purpose may be more important than my little rebellion. The Queen left these soldiers here for a reason, and I have just discovered that their presence may be the only thing keeping something imprisoned.
But I think of the Father. The ritual. The prisoners. Blake. And I think of the altar, with those terrible words written upon the stone. CONSENT: UNNECESSARY. If I turn back now, I may never get another chance. I look at Peter.
“I'm sorry.”
He says nothing, but his fingers tighten around his spear.
“Keep going, men. We have to stop the Father. Then I'll get you back to your positions.”
I raise my scepter.
“Charge!”
The Spirit of Halloween surges through me. The skeletons obey. They cross the circle, trampling the ancient seal beneath hundreds of rattling feet. Bones scrape against stone. The markings flare beneath them, a pale light spilling through the cracks. Something deep below the chamber groans. The entire room trembles. A sound rises from the floor, like a thousand people drawing breath at once. Peter stumbles. I catch his arm.
“Keep moving!”
We rush toward the far passage. Behind us, the light in the seal dims. One of the old carvings splits down the middle. And something behind the stone takes a slow, heavy breath. I do not look back. We reach another chamber, somewhat larger than the last, where fresh air slips through cracks in the ceiling. I can smell the garden above, damp soil and midnight roses We are close. I can feel it. But the Girl's voice follows me.
“Don't go yet.”
I stop.
“Oh, what now?”
“It's not ready.”
“Are you telling me what to do? Everyone does that.”
“This is for your own good. Just trust me.”
“That's what everybody says right before something terrible happens.”
“I want this ritual intercepted, too.”
I narrow my eyes.
“You do?”
“To an extent.”
“That's reassuring.”
“Scout the area. Give me time to put a few things in place. We can attack together.”
I hesitate. Then I ask the question that has been bothering me.
“What about Blake?”
The walls fall silent. For a moment, I hear only the faint dripping of water.
“He has his own choices to make,” she finally whispers.
The stone ahead begins to pale, the shadows dissolving as the Girl withdraws from the walls. I look at Peter. He looks at me. Neither of us says anything. Well, Peter can't. I suppose that makes two of us.
“Right,” I mutter. “Time to plan.”
I point toward a small group of soldiers.
“Slight men, Peter, and you... uh... Paul. Yes, follow me.”
Paul raises his hand.
“The rest of you, Ruban, you're in charge. Stay here, watch the passage, and don't do anything.”
Ruban nods. I have absolutely no idea if that's actually his name. The skeletons seem restless. Crossing the seal has clearly upset them, and I can't blame them. They've spent centuries waiting for their Queen, only to discover that the first thing their returning monarch does is trample the very duty they were left to perform.
I'll fix things soon. I hope. We find a narrow passage leading upward, and eventually emerge into the garden. The midnight roses are in full bloom. Their petals are black at the edges, silvered by the pale light pouring through the broken roof. The air is cold and smells faintly of rain, although no rain has fallen.
We move carefully among the hedges, keeping low, our bones rattling whenever a branch catches our armor. Beyond the garden, the sanctuary hall has almost been completely rebuilt. I peek through a gap in the bushes. The walls have been patched with fresh stone. The pews are back in place, their broken fittings repaired with strips of metal and twisted silk. The holy relics have been arranged on tables along the walls.
But the altar…
Oh, the altar.
It has been transformed. The old altar has been stripped of its decorations and replaced with a broad, dark stone platform, its surface carved with rings and grooves that converge upon a central hollow. A sacrificial table. I wonder who that is for.
Above the sanctuary, strange lights drift through the ruined roof. The Spirits of Halloween flutter around the towers, their glowing pumpkin faces bobbing in the darkness, laughing as they weave through the rafters like children playing at a circus.
The laughter is wrong. Too cheerful. Too eager.
Down below, prisoners continue their work, carrying relics and arranging candles, their movements slow and strangely synchronized.
I spot Blake.
He's talking to the Warden.
“Say, Warden,” he says, scratching his waxy chin, “when all this is done, what are you going to do? Retire? Keep an eye on us? Take a nice long nap?”
“Certainly,” Calva mutters, instructing another prisoner to move a relic closer to the altar. “I'll do as the good Father wills. Don't you worry, my dear Wax Man.”
Blake hesitates.
“Do you think he could... get my skin back?”
Calva stops.
“And my memories?”
She looks at him.
“The good ones,” he adds quickly. “Not the fiery ones.”
For a moment, I think she's going to brush him aside. Instead, she takes his hand.
“I don't know,” she says softly. “Only what the Father wills. But hold my hand, dear.”
Blake glances down at their hands. Then he closes his eye. Calva begins to pray. Her words are too quiet for me to hear, but I see her lips moving, her fingers tightening around his. A faint glow gathers between them.
The candles flicker.
Blake's shoulders begin to tremble. And then…
A child's laughter. Soft. Clear. Beautiful. It drifts through the sanctuary, and for one terrible moment, even I feel the urge to smile. Blake opens his eyes.
“Her,” he whispers.
His voice breaks.
“She was so sweet. So pure. I remember her voice.”
He presses his free hand against his mouth.
“That's her. That's my little girl.”
Calva watches him carefully.
“I wish I knew more about her,” Blake continues, his eyes shining. “I wish I knew her name. But that... that was wonderful, dear Sister. Thank you.”
He laughs, a small, disbelieving sound, and wipes at his face.
“I haven't felt that happy in... I don't even know how long.”
The Warden pats his shoulder.
“You're welcome, my dear.”
Blake looks at her.
“If you need anything from me, just give the word.”
Calva's smile grows.
“As a matter of fact, I have big plans for you.”
She gestures toward the altar.
“Your body may be particularly useful during the ritual. The Father will need the relics arranged in a certain order, and your wax can hold things in place where ordinary materials would fail. You'll help me move them when asked.”
Blake glances at the table.
“And after?”
“Perhaps you'll remember more.”
“Perhaps?”
“Perhaps you'll be made whole.”
He studies her face. Then he nods.
“Alright, Sister. I'll help.”
I stare through the bushes. I've never seen Blake so happy. And I hate that. Not because he deserves to suffer, but because I know how easy it is to mistake a beautiful memory for a promise. The Father has offered him something real. And Blake has chosen to follow that hope. He isn't doing it for me. He isn't doing it for the Girl.He's doing it for himself. And I can't blame him.
“What's the plan?” I whisper.
Peter and Paul shrug. Of course. I slump back into the bushes, feeling defeated. Somewhere nearby, a prisoner is cooing lovingly at a pile of bones. Femur Finder. Naturally. I close my eyes for a moment. Plans rarely go as planned.
The Father seems to know what's going on, the Warden is too busy, and the Girl is off doing whatever strange thing she thinks is for my own good.
My army is waiting. The ritual is almost ready. And I'm sitting in a bush.
“Wonderful.”
I stand.
“Boys, we get one chance. One. We wait until the right moment, then we attack.”
Peter immediately begins marching toward the sanctuary. Paul grabs his arm and pulls him back. Peter turns toward him. Paul shakes his skull. I point at them.
“Exactly. Not yet. We need the others, and we need word from the Girl.”
Peter reluctantly steps back. For once, I'm glad somebody in this army has a little patience. We slip back into the hidden passages, keeping to the shadows, and wait. Time crawls.
The candles burn lower.
Somewhere above us, the Spirits of Halloween continue their strange aerial celebration, their laughter echoing through the palace. Then I hear footsteps.
Click.
Clack.
Click.
Clack.
The Warden.
We peer through a crack in the stone as she passes, her billhook tapping against the floor, her dark cloak dragging behind her. She is humming. That alone is enough to worry me. Calva doesn't hum. Not unless she's planning something dreadful. We follow her through a narrow corridor until she reaches her office. The door closes.
We creep toward a nearby window, cracked open just enough for me to hear her voice. She's praying. Or speaking to someone. Perhaps both.
“We are so close to ready,” she whispers. “The skeleton will return soon, just as you foretold.”
A pause.
“Yes.”
Another pause.
“No. No, we can't.”
Her voice grows quieter.
“Yes. He will be complete.”
I lean closer.
“Changed. Different. Better. A true Spirit of Halloween once again.”
My ribs tighten around the ember. The Spirit stirs. Calva continues.
“No, I'm not to question you.”
Silence.
Then…
“Through the suffering, he'll be stable. Complete. Better.”
I glance at Peter. He is watching the window. Calva's voice trembles.
“Change the past? Are you sure? You are very good at that.”
A long silence. Then she whispers:
“Yes.”
And finally:
“What is one more ring for the bell?”
I freeze. The prayer ends. Something shifts inside the office. I carefully peer through the window. Calva is sitting on the floor, her head bowed, her hands pressed together so tightly that her knuckles have gone pale. She looks exhausted. Not simply tired.
Exhausted in the way a person looks after carrying something heavy for so long that they've forgotten what it feels like to stand without it. For a moment, I almost feel sorry for her.
Then she rises.
She begins gathering objects from her desk, placing them into a small leather pouch. A key. A little bundle of bones. A strip of black cloth.
And the collar off in the distance, away from her. I recognized it immediately. The very same collar that once took my body away from me. But something is wrong. It isn't lying on the desk. It's already fastened around the neck of the lion gargoyle. The stone creature sits motionless beside the window, its wings folded against its back, its eyes fixed on nothing.
Calva doesn't even look at it. She passes within arm's reach. The gargoyle's stone tail twitches. Just once. Calva continues packing. I stare. What in the world? The collar's metal links glimmer faintly, and for a moment, I see a thin shadow moving beneath the stone surface of the gargoyle's throat.
A little hand.
Then it's gone.
The skeletons lower me from the window. I land awkwardly, my armor clattering.
“She's getting ready,” I whisper. “And she's not waiting for us.”
Peter points toward the sanctuary.
“Right. Let's get ready to put on a show.”
I glance back at the gargoyle. It hasn't moved again. I tell myself it's nothing. A statue. A trick of the light. A little stone lion with a very suspicious fashion accessory. I really need to stop lying to myself.
We return to the hidden chamber. The remaining skeletons are gathered around the passage, looking increasingly confused and restless.
Ruban is sitting on a coffin. Someone has stolen his spear. Two others are arguing over a skull that may or may not belong to either of them.Then I hear it.
Tap.
Tap.
Tap.
The sound comes from the walls.
The Iron Maiden.
I feel the cold creep through my bones.
The tapping moves.
Tap.
Tap.
Tap.
It travels along the passage, sometimes ahead of us, sometimes behind us, as though something is moving through the walls themselves.
I press my hand against the stone. My echoes flicker. A massive shape glides through the darkness beyond the wall. Chains. Rust. A faint green light burning inside a chest of iron. The Iron Maiden. But it isn't wandering aimlessly. It's following something. A trail. A scent.
A magical trace that moves through the walls like a thin silver thread.
The thread leads upward. Toward the sanctuary. Toward the Warden's office. Toward the gargoyle. I pull my hand away.
“Peter.”
He looks at me.
“Is the Maiden following the Girl?”
Peter stares at the wall. Then he slowly nods.
Oh.
That's unsettling. And I suddenly understand why the journal's warning was written the way it was.
THE MAIDEN REMEMBERS.
THE BROTHER CALLS.
THE SISTER WAITS.
Whatever remains of the brother inside that monster is searching for her. And she's walking straight toward it. I turn toward the army.
“Listen carefully.”
The skeletons gather around me.
“When the time is right, you will know. Spread out around the sanctuary. Attack whoever tries to stop me. Peter will guide you. Follow his orders.”
They look confused. A few raise their weapons. One scratches its skull. I sigh.
“Just... try not to die again.”
They nod. I leave the rest to Peter and slip through the passage alone. The sanctuary hall is quiet when I enter. Too quiet. Every prisoner is seated in the pews, their faces turned toward the altar. Some sit perfectly still, others rock gently back and forth, whispering prayers I cannot understand.
The air is thick with incense. Underneath it is another smell. Burnt sugar.
Blake.
A church organ begins to play. The notes are slow and solemn, drifting through the sanctuary like a funeral procession. A choir of prisoners and hidden Spirits of Halloween begins singing.
Huh.
Spider Duchess can sing.
Strange.
Her voice is beautiful, actually, a thin, haunting melody that seems to come from somewhere deep underground. The choir sings of repentance. Of restoration. Of things returned to their proper places. I creep along the back wall, keeping to the shadows.
Then the sanctuary doors open. The Warden enters. Slowly.
Click.
Clack.
Click.
Clack.
Every head turns toward her. She walks to the altar, her billhook tapping against the stone, and raises one hand. The organ stops. The choir falls silent.
“Penitence is at hand,” she announces. “Soon, the skeleton will arrive, on Halloween night. Soon, you will all be made complete. The Father wills it!”
The prisoners roar in approval. Blake stands beside her, clapping along. He looks happier than I've ever seen him. For a moment, I hesitate. Maybe he's right. Maybe the Father can give him his life back. Maybe all of this suffering really can end. Then I see the altar. The hollow at its center. The chains. The old carvings. And I remember the words.
CONSENT: UNNECESSARY.
No. Not like this. I step out of the shadows.
“There will be no trial tonight, you Spirit! I'm not going to let you!”
The congregation gasps. Hundreds of eyes turn toward me. Calva smiles.
“There you are.”
Her voice is almost affectionate.
“The Father said you were close.”
I raise my scepter.
“Stay away from me.”
“Come to me, my child. Let us make you whole again.”
The words slide through the sanctuary, soft and warm, like a lullaby whispered over a grave.

text:
Daily Pilgrimage to Purgatory: Saturday.
.
Preparation: Either one of the following acts or similar one will suffice:
.
Prayer. 
.
O St. Margaret Mary, whom the Lord has chosen to reveal to the whole world all the treasures hidden in His merciful Heart of Love! O thou who hast heard how the Poor Souls in Purgatory begged for this new remedy, the devotion to the Sacred Heart which relieves them so effectively of their torments! O thou who hast set free so many of these poor prisoners by practicing this devotion: obtain for us the grace to make this Pilgrimage worthily in the company of the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Amen. Unite your own intentions with those of the faithful who make this pilgrimage daily.
.
Consecration of the Day:
.
Divine Heart of Jesus, in making this pilgrimage with Thee as my Companion, I consecrate to Thee all my thoughts, words and actions of the entire day. I pray Thee to unite my small merits with Thine and to apply them to the Poor Souls, especially the soul of Thy servant, NN______.
Likewise do I entreat you, holy souls, to help me obtain the grace to persevere in love and loyalty toward the Sacred Heart, by submitting readily and without complaint to whatever designs He may have in my regard.
.
Offering:
.
Eternal Father, we offer Thee the Blood, Passion and Death of Jesus Christ, and the sorrows of the most holy Mary and St. Joseph, in payment for our sins, in suffrage for the holy souls in Purgatory, for the wants of our Holy Mother the Church, and for the conversion of sinners. Amen.
.
Ejaculations:
.
"May the Sacred Heart of Jesus be loved everywhere."
"Our Lady of the Sacred Heart, pray for us."
"St. Joseph, model and patron of those who love the Sacred Heart, pray for us."
.
Preparatory Meditation: 
.
Let us for a moment, in company with the Sacred Heart, descend in spirit into the consuming flames of Purgatory. How many of these souls are beginning their painful imprisonment this very moment! How many of them have been there for a long t:me and shall be there for a longer time to come! And what a holy legion, almost entirely purified and cleansed at the present moment, shall rise to heaven this very day! How happy the Poor Souls are! They have escaped hell forever. They are certain to obtain eternal happiness. They are friends of God; they are saved. And yet, how miserable they are at the same time. They must still suffer temporal punishment for sins which have been already forgiven them. The gates of their heavenly fatherland are still closed to them; they are sentenced to expiating fire. Behold them in their present plight! Listen to their lamentations! Speak to them a word of friendship and sympathy, and hasten to their assistance!
.
Saturday
.
Holy Souls in Purgatory, is there anything you regret when you think of your life on earth?  I deeply regret the little amount of charity I have shown towards the Poor Souls during my life on earth ... I could have been of such great service to them, since a Catholic can bring so much light and peace to these poor, suffering prisoners. I could have helped them by my prayers, mortifications, alms, good works, holy Communions and holy Masses, the latter, either by having them said for the Poor Souls or by attending them, especially those celebrated in honor of the Sacred Heart. I would have obtained numerous graces which would have made it easier for me to avoid sin.  Moreover, I would have deserved a much shorter and less painful Purgatory, and now I would receive a much greater share in the prayers which were said for us wherever there are Catholics.  Oh, could I but return to the world to help the Poor Souls! I certainly would interest myself in their sad plight! What devout prayers would I say for them! How solicitous I would be to awaken in the faithful the most tender sympathy and pity for them!
.
Pious Exercises:
.
Resolution.
.
Today I will do everything possible to assist the souls of the faithful departed from the mission fields of Melanesia and Micronesia (New Ireland, New Britain, the Solomon, Gilben and Marshall Islands and New Guinea).  I also recommend myself to those who are entering heaven at this moment.
.
Thought for the day.
.
Thus spoke the guilt-burdened brothers of innocent Joseph one to another: "We deserve to suffer these things, because we have sinned against out brother, seeing the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore, is this affliction come upon us." (Gen. 42, 21).
.
Exercise.
.
Spread, as much as possible, the devotion "Daily Pilgrimage to Purgatory."  The Poor Souls will be grateful to you.
.
Special Intention.
.
Pray for the soul which had the greatest devotion to Out Lady of the Sacred Heart.
.
Motive.
.
In doing so you cause the Mother of God great delight; she will obtain for you, through the intercession of this soul, the grace of a true devotion to the Sacred Heart.
.
Prayer.
.
O Lord God Almighty, I beseech Thee, by the Precious Blood, which gushed forth from the side of Thy Divine Son Jesus, in the sight of, and to the extreme pain of His most holy Mother, deliver the souls in Purgatory, and especially that soul which was the most devout to Our Lady of the Sacred Heart and Queen of Heaven; that it may soon attain unto Thy glory, there to praise Thee in her, and her in Thee, world without end. Amen.
.
Our Father, Hail Mary.
.
Ejaculation.
.
Our Lady of the Sacred Heart, pray for us!
.
The Daily Pilgrimage continues to Sunday again.

text:
The solution by $GOOG? Leave Earth 🌎 behind.

With Project Suncatcher, $GOOG is exploring a radical system design: a massive, scalable AI infrastructure built entirely in space. By launching constellations of solar-powered satellites equipped with their custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), $GOOG aims to unlock a new frontier for computing.

Here is why this "moonshot" could be the strategic game changer that redefines the future of AI. 👇

1. Unlocking Infinite, Clean Energy: The most immediate advantage of space is energy. On Earth, solar power is limited by weather, atmosphere, and the simple fact that the sun sets every night. In the dawn-dusk sun-synchronous low Earth orbit (LEO) proposed by Project Suncatcher, satellites face near-constant sunlight.

$GOOG notes that a solar panel in this specific orbit can be up to eight times more productive than one on Earth. This means a continuous, battery-free power supply for power-hungry AI workloads. By moving the energy consumption to space, $GOOG can scale its compute capabilities indefinitely without putting further strain on Earth’s fragile energy grids.

2. The "Data Center in the Sky" Design: The technical brilliance of Project Suncatcher lies in how it mimics a terrestrial data center in a vacuum.

3. Close-Formation Flying: To achieve the lightning-fast data transfer speeds required for training AI (tens of terabits per second), the satellites won't be lonely outposts. They will fly in tight clusters, mere kilometers or even hundreds of meters apart.

4. Free-Space Optical Links: Instead of fiber optic cables, these satellites will communicate using laser links (Free-Space Optical communication). Because light travels faster in a vacuum than through glass fiber, this setup potentially offers lower latency and massive bandwidth.

5. Radiation-Hardy Hardware: One of the biggest fears regarding space computing is radiation. However, $GOOG has already stress-tested its Trillium (v6e) TPUs with proton beams, finding them surprisingly resilient. The hardware held up to radiation doses far exceeding a standard five-year mission, proving that off-the-shelf AI chips can survive the harsh environment of LEO.

6. Escaping Terrestrial Bottlenecks: Building new data centers on Earth is becoming a logistical nightmare. You need vast plots of land, millions of gallons of water for cooling, and access to local power grids that are already overtaxed.

Project Suncatcher bypasses these physical bottlenecks entirely. There is no land to buy, no neighbors to disturb, and cooling, while technically challenging in a vacuum can be managed through radiative designs. This allows $GOOG to scale its infrastructure at a pace that terrestrial construction simply cannot match.

7. The Economic Tipping Point: Historically, the cost of putting mass into orbit made ideas like this impossible. But the space economy is shifting rapidly. Google’s analysis suggests that with launch prices projected to drop below $200/kg by the mid-2030s (thanks to reusable rockets like @SpaceX Starship), the cost of a space-based data center could eventually rival the energy costs of a ground-based one. 👇

text:
Alexander Orlov (1895-1973) was a high-ranking Soviet secret police (NKVD) officer and spy whose dramatic life and defection became one of the most famous stories of 20th-century espionage....

As the NKVD resident spy in Republican Spain, Orlov oversaw the secret transport of Spain's massive gold reserves (about 500 tons) to Moscow in exchange for Soviet military aid. He also managed counterintelligence operations and purges against anti-Stalinist and Trotskyite factions. During Joseph Stalin's Great Terror, Orlov grew terrified that he would be recalled to the USSR and executed like many of his peers. He fled with his wife and daughter to Canada and then the United States. Before leaving, he reportedly took tens of thousands of dollars in operational funds and left a letter warning Stalin that if his family was harmed, he would publish secret files. Orlov lived quietly underground in the U.S. for years, eventually revealing his identity and publishing his landmark 1953 book, The Secret History of Stalin's Crimes. The book offered unprecedented insider details about the Moscow show trials and Stalin's inner circle. Later in life, he worked as a research fellow at the University of Michigan before dying in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1973.

. . . . 

A coded telegram marked with highest-priority security ciphers landed on a desk in Paris on July 9, 1938, instructing a Soviet major general to report immediately to the port of Antwerp. Major General Alexander Orlov, the supreme rezident of the NKVD in Spain, was directed to board the Soviet transport ship Svir for an urgent, confidential operational conference. To an untrained officer, it read like a routine administrative summons. To Orlov, who had spent two decades inside the inner gears of the Bolshevik secret police, the telegram was a death warrant. Across Europe and Moscow, veteran intelligence rezidents who stepped onto Soviet ships or boarded trains home were being handcuffed in the corridors, dragged to the cellars of the Lubyanka, and shot in the back of the neck. Instead of boarding the ship, the man who held the Kremlin’s darkest international secrets withdrew sixty thousand dollars in operational cash, bought steamship tickets under a forged passport, and vanished into thin air.

For the preceding two years, Orlov had served as Joseph Stalin’s personal viceroy in the Spanish Civil War. Dispatched to Madrid in September 1936 as chief Soviet security advisor to the Second Spanish Republic, Orlov wielded terrifying, unaccountable power. Operating out of safe houses and disguised legations, he oversaw the liquidation of anti-Stalinist leftists, orchestrating the abduction and brutal murder of POUM leader Andreu Nin. Most famously, Orlov masterminded one of the greatest financial transfers in modern history: the extraction of the "Moscow Gold." Over three nights in October 1936, under naval escort, he coordinated the loading of five hundred and ten metric tons of the Spanish Republic’s gold reserves onto four Soviet freighters bound for Odessa, delivering over seventy percent of Spain's entire national treasury directly into Stalin's vaults. There was virtually no foreign black operation Orlov had not supervised.

Yet as the Great Terror devoured the Soviet security apparatus, proximity to the dictator became a fatal liability. NKVD chief Nikolai Yezhov was systematically liquidating every overseas operative who knew too much. Orlov watched as his former superiors, friends, and colleagues—men like Abram Slutsky and Yan Berzin—disappeared into execution cellars. Defectors like Ignace Reiss, who broke with the regime in Switzerland, were tracked down by Soviet wet-affairs commandos and machine-gunned on country roads. Orlov knew that fleeing was nearly impossible; the NKVD maintained an international reach with assassins stationed across the globe.

text:
BEFORE THE MAPS CHANGED

The Hand of Irulegi, the Atlantic, and the People Who May Have Left Before the Waters Rose

What if the people of a vanished homeland did not escape its destruction?

What if they had already left?

Our investigation at The Ark Initiative began with a single word: 
SORIONEKU, inscribed on a bronze hand discovered at Irulegi, an Iron Age settlement in what is now Navarre, Spain. The hand was found near a household entrance. Researchers have proposed a connection between its opening word and the modern Basque expression for good fortune, although the full inscription remains disputed.

A hand at a doorway. A possible blessing. A community leaving a message at the threshold between home and the wider world.

That object led us to ask a larger question: who made such symbols, who carried them, and how far did their knowledge travel?

The Atlantic coastline of the distant past was not the coastline we know today. During the last ice age, sea levels were much lower. As the world warmed, rising water transformed coastal plains, estuaries, and places where people could have lived. Some of the landscapes we need to investigate are now underwater.

We began looking beyond the familiar story of a civilization destroyed in a single catastrophe. 
Maritime communities could have traded, migrated, married, and established new settlements generations,or centuries,  before a homeland was lost.
 Their descendants might preserve fragments of language, craft, ritual, and memory without ever witnessing its final disappearance.

That possibility brings us to the Basques. Euskara is a remarkable surviving non-Indo-European language. Archaeology and ancient DNA provide evidence of deep regional continuity, while the Hand of Irulegi offers a rare, tangible window into ancient Vasconic expression. Neither proves descent from Plato's Atlantis. But together they give us real places, artifacts, and timelines against which to test an Atlantic migration hypothesis.

We also follow copper and bronze craftsmanship, exchange routes, protective hands, animal imagery, and the blue stone lapis lazuli. In the Epic of Gilgamesh, a goddess invokes her lapis ornament after the flood, refusing to forget the dead. In Genesis, the rainbow becomes a promise concerning the future of living creatures. These are different traditions, yet both ask how a promise survives destruction.

Our research does not begin by declaring that every resemblance has one origin.
 It begins by tracing the people, the coastlines, the objects, and the dates, and by asking what survived when the maps changed.

Read the full research paper and watch the film:

text:
RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/qp11S5pjv3 | Author: @militarnyi Rafale M Carrier-Based Fighter Made First Landing on Indian Aircraft Carrier INS Vikrant 
A Rafale M carrier-based fighter jet landed on the Indian aircraft carrier INS Vikrant for the first time. The French fighters are set to replace the Russian MiG-29K/KUBs, which currently form the backbone of the country’s carrier-based aviation.

The Indian Navy press office reported the successful landing.

According to the Navy, the aircraft successfully landed on the deck on its first attempt on October 29, 2026. The Navy noted that this marked “the first steps toward putting the aircraft into service” with the fleet.

According to the publication Defence Security Asia, the landing was performed by a French Navy aircraft piloted by a French pilot.

A Rafale Marine aircraft successfully landed onboard #IndianNavy’s indigenous Aircraft Carrier #INSVikrant on its maiden attempt on 29 Oct 26.

The ongoing trials mark the first steps towards operationalisation of the aircraft in the #IndianNavy. https://t.co/IJf6l4wCN3

— SpokespersonNavy (@indiannavy) October 30, 2026

The tests on the aircraft carrier provided real-world conditions to verify whether the French carrier-based fighter is capable of meeting Indian requirements outside the controlled environment of a land-based test facility.

Typically, Rafale M aircraft operate from the French aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle, using a catapult for takeoff and an arresting gear for landing. In contrast, INS Vikrant and INS Vikramaditya employ a short takeoff and landing (STOL) scheme with arresting gear: the aircraft accelerates using its own engine thrust and then rolls over the ski-jump ramp.

Since the ski-jump alters the aircraft’s takeoff trajectory from the deck but does not provide the additional acceleration offered by a catapult, a safe takeoff depends on the aircraft’s weight, available thrust, takeoff run length, and external conditions. Preliminary tests at the ground facility at Hansa Air Base in Goa demonstrated the feasibility of takeoff from a ski-jump ramp.

Rafale M in India

In April 2025, India signed an agreement with France worth approximately $7.5 billion for the supply of 26 Rafale aircraft for naval aviation, specifically for use on the aircraft carrier INS Vikrant.

 A Rafale M carrier-based fighter of the French Navy. Photo credits: French Navy

Under the agreement, the Indian Naval Aviation will receive 26 Rafale fighters, four of which will be in a two-seat configuration not intended for operation from aircraft carriers. They will be used exclusively at land-based airfields during training exercises and to maintain pilot proficiency.

The French aircraft are set to replace the Russian MiG-29K/KUB fighters in the Indian Naval Aviation, which currently form the backbone of the country’s carrier-based aviation but face serious issues regarding reliability and build quality.

 A MiG-29K deck-mounted fighter aircraft of the Indian Navy. 2020. Photo from open sources

The first aircraft are expected to be delivered between mid-2028 and the end of 2028 or early 2029, with deliveries expected to be completed around 2030–2031.

In February 2026, it was reported that India plans to place an additional order for 31 Rafale M fighters in addition to the 26 aircraft previously contracted. If these plans are carried out, the total number of Rafale aircraft ordered for the Indian Navy will increase to 57.

Ed Miliband lecturing the public on “having the bravery to have honest conversations about our history” is a masterclass in performative Westminster cowardice. His selective version of honesty carefully edits out the historical facts that undermine the establishment narrative of perpetual national guilt.  

An honest conversation would acknowledge that ordinary British taxpayers only finished paying off the monumental twenty million pound debt incurred under the 1833 Slavery Abolition Act in 2015. For nearly two centuries, working-class households financed the eradication of the trade through their taxes. An honest history would remember the Royal Navy West Africa Squadron, where thousands of British sailors died of yellow fever and combat while hunting down slaver vessels on the high seas, or the destitute Lancashire mill workers who chose starvation over touching slave-grown American cotton in 1862. None of these sacrifices ever feature in ministerial speeches because Whitehall is incapable of celebrating working-class moral backbone.

The glaring irony is Miliband’s own parliamentary record. While he expects the British public to prostrate themselves over historic sins, his own bravery evaporates the second he is faced with the Crown. Throughout his career, Miliband has reliably backed the Sovereign Grant to safeguard royal finances and repeatedly taken to the dispatch box to shower the monarchy with reverent adulation. He praised the royal household for embodying a “quiet, dignified sense of duty” and hailed the Queen as “our nation’s constant” while formally offering his “loyalty and devotion” to the Crown.

The institution he lavished with uncritical praise is the very entity that granted the royal monopoly charter to the Royal African Company under King Charles II and James Stuart. Yet rather than having the courage to scrutinise the historic wealth of the Crown itself, Miliband waved through royal funding settlements and led his benches in choruses of “God save the King.”

Dumping retroactive imperial guilt onto ordinary Britons whose ancestors were toiling twelve hours a day in northern coal mines and cotton mills, while voting to preserve the financial privileges of the Crown, is classic SW1 hypocrisy. Preaching contrition at an international summit while passing the moral bill to your own taxpayers is not an act of courage; it is the cheapest form of virtue-signalling on offer.

text:
🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Days 190 to 196 (Week 28): Phase Three: Welcome to the Third Trimester
📚 Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. To maintain medical accuracy, every lesson is fact-checked by Grok (Sal). General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.
✨ Welcome to the third trimester, the home stretch. Your baby can now blink. From this week, many doctors ask you to notice your baby's movements every day, because those kicks are your baby's way of saying, "I'm here." Do you know what your baby's normal looks like?

🌱 This week: the third trimester begins. Your baby can open and close the eyes and blink, the brain keeps growing fast, and fat keeps building. Your baby is about 15 inches from head to heel and weighs about 2 1/4 pounds, about the size of an eggplant.

👶 Where your baby is this week
If conception happened around day 14, your baby is 176 to 182 days old this week. Last week brought hiccups and rhythm. This week the final season begins.
Your baby can open and close the eyes and blink. Eyelashes are in place. The brain keeps adding cells and folds, and fat keeps building under the skin.
Your baby is about 15 inches from head to heel and weighs about 2 1/4 pounds. Over the next 12 weeks, your baby's weight will more than triple.

🤰 Your body this week
Prenatal visits now usually come every two weeks. If your blood is Rh-negative, this is often when you get the Rh shot. Ask about the Tdap vaccine too.
Ask your doctor how to track your baby's movements. Call your doctor or midwife right away if your baby moves much less than usual, or for regular tightenings, bleeding, leaking fluid, a severe headache, changes in your vision, or sudden swelling.

🎵 Why singing, not talking
Talking needs understanding. Singing is melody, rhythm, and pitch, and those can be received before understanding arrives. Hearing usually begins between about Week 18 and Week 26, and word meaning comes after birth. From conception your baby is a spirit being, and GUP songs go spirit to spirit.
GUP songs are baby music with a purpose: gentle like lullabies, repeating like nursery rhymes, and full of phonic songs the whole family can sing. This is your child's first kids music.

🔤 Phase Three: action words
This week, sing action words. "Sing." "Pray." "Hug." "Kiss." "Sleep." These are the things your family will do with your baby every day. Build each from your First Sounds list and sing it on the melody.

🎶 One song, three ways
Morning: hear the Week-28 song and thank God for the third trimester. Midday: hum it with headphones on, then sing "hug" and "kiss" to the tune. Evening: write your action words on your Word List page with their phonograms.
Dad, headphones on you too. Sing "pray" with her each night.

🙏 Pray and remember
📖 “Behold, I am accomplishing new things. And presently, they will spring forth. With certainty, you will know them.” (Isaiah 43:19, CPDV)
🎂 John Quincy Adams was born July 11, 1767. His mother, Abigail, taught him at home during the Revolutionary War, and he grew up to become the sixth president of the United States.
"Father God, thank You for bringing us into the final season. Finish the good work You began in our child. In Jesus' name, amen."

✅ This week's quick checklist
Prenatal vitamin every day. Noticed my baby's movements. Asked about the Rh shot and Tdap. Heard, hummed, and wrote this week's song. Sang action words. Dad sang along. Next week: Growing Strong.

🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Deep Dive: Week 28 (Days 190 to 196): Phase Three: Welcome to the Third Trimester

🗓️ Week 28 at a Glance
Week 28 is pregnancy days 190 to 196, counted from the first day of your last period, the same way your doctor, midwife, and pregnancy calculator count. If conception happened around day 14, your baby is between 176 and 182 days old. In longer or shorter cycles, these days shift a little.
This week the third trimester begins. It runs from Week 28 until birth. Your baby can now open and close the eyes and blink. The brain is growing quickly, fat keeps building, and the lungs keep maturing. Your baby's movements are strong, and from now on they are an important sign of your baby's well-being.
Your baby is about 15 inches from head to heel and weighs about 2 1/4 pounds, about the size of an eggplant. Between now and birth, most babies more than triple their weight.

🗓️ The Week, Day by Day
Here is the week counted in days after conception. In a 28-day cycle, add 14 to find your pregnancy day. Babies grow at their own pace, so use this as a guide.
Days 176 and 177 (pregnancy days 190 and 191): Your baby opens and closes the eyes and blinks. Eyelashes are in place.
Days 178 and 179 (days 192 and 193): The brain keeps adding cells and connections, and its surface folds more deeply.
Day 180 (day 194): Fat continues to build under the skin, helping your baby fill out.
Day 181 (day 195): The lungs keep adding air sacs and making more surfactant.
Day 182 (day 196): Your baby weighs about 2 1/4 pounds and is about 15 inches from head to heel.

🎉 The Home Stretch
The third trimester is the season of finishing. In the first trimester, God laid down every organ. In the second, He shaped the face, opened the ears, and built strength. Now, in the third, He fills out what He has made.
Your baby will gain most of the birth weight in these weeks. The lungs will finish getting ready. The brain will grow at an amazing pace. Fat will build up to keep your baby warm after birth.
You are in this season too. Your body will work harder than ever. You may feel tired, heavy, and uncomfortable. But every heavy step is carrying your child closer to the day you meet. The apostle Paul wrote that the One who began a good work will carry it to completion. God does not leave His work half-done.
📖 “I am confident of this very thing: that he who has begun this good work in you will perfect it, unto the day of Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 1:6, CPDV)
🎂 Sidney Poitier was born February 20, 1927. Born two months early and so small that few expected him to live, he grew up to become the first Black man to win the Academy Award for Best Actor.

👁️ Blinking Eyes
Your baby can now open the eyes, close them, and blink. Eyelashes frame them. The eyes respond to changes in light that pass through your belly.
The parts of the brain that handle vision keep developing all through the third trimester and the first year. At birth, your baby will see shapes, light and dark, and faces up close. Over the first months, vision will grow sharper and colors will come in.
When your baby is born, hold your baby close and let those eyes find your face. Sing the weekly song. Your face and your voice will meet your baby's eyes and ears together.
📖 “For you have possessed my temperament. You have supported me from my mother’s womb.” (Psalm 138:13, CPDV; 139:13 KJV)

🦶 Paying Attention to Movement
From about Week 28, your baby's movements become one of the best signs of how your baby is doing. Many doctors ask mothers to notice movement every day and to know their baby's normal pattern.
A common way is to pick a time when your baby is usually active, often after a meal or in the evening. Sit or lie on your side and count kicks, rolls, and jabs. Many doctors use 10 movements as a guide, and most babies reach that within two hours, often much sooner. Ask your doctor how they want you to do it.
What matters most is your baby's normal. If your baby is moving much less than usual, do not wait until tomorrow. Call your doctor or midwife right away, even at night. Do not rely on a home heartbeat monitor to reassure you. Your doctor can check your baby properly.
Make the weekly song part of your counting time. Put on your headphones, sing softly, and count the kicks that answer.
📖 “I know it at first light; great is your faithfulness.” (Lamentations 3:23, CPDV)
🎂 Luciano Pavarotti was born October 12, 1935. As a boy he sang in the church choir alongside his father, a baker, and practiced every day for years to become one of the most famous tenors of all time.

🧠 Billions of Brain Cells
Your baby's brain is growing at an amazing pace. Billions of brain cells are in place, and new connections between them form every day. The surface of the brain is folding more deeply to fit it all inside the skull.
In the third trimester, the brain grows faster than at any other time in pregnancy. Much of that growth will keep going after birth. By the first birthday, your baby's brain will be more than twice its size at birth.
Good food, rest, and avoiding harmful substances all help. So does the world your baby lives in. Familiar voices, gentle songs, and a calm home are part of the environment where this brain grows.

🫁 Lungs Getting Closer
Your baby's lungs are still not finished, but they are much further along than a few weeks ago. More air sacs are forming, more surfactant is being made, and the blood vessels around the air sacs are growing closer.
Babies born this early need special care in a neonatal intensive care unit, often with help to breathe. Each week in the womb now makes a real difference to how ready the lungs will be.
This is why doctors take signs of early labor so seriously in the third trimester. Know the signs, and call right away if you notice them.
Keep your daily lullabies and phonic songs going. Calm, steady singing helps you rest, and rest helps your body carry your baby well.

🔤 Phase Three: Action Words
Phase Three has given you family words, food words, face words, sound words, praise words, light words, and clapped beats. This week, sing action words. These are words for things your family does: "sing," "pray," "hug," "kiss," "rock," "sleep," "eat," "walk."
Build each one from your First Sounds list. "Sing" is "s," "i," "ng." "Hug" is "h," "u," "g." "Kiss" is "k," "i," "ss." "Pray" is "p," "r," "ay." Sing each word slowly on the melody of the weekly song and clap its beats.
After birth, these words will come alive. You will sing "hug" as you hug your baby, "kiss" as you kiss those cheeks, "rock" as you rock in the chair. Words joined to actions are some of the first words a child understands. These little phonic songs are baby music, lullabies, nursery rhymes, and kids music, all built into the life of your home.
📖 “Write the vision and explain it on tablets.” (Habakkuk 2:2, CPDV)
🎂 Jim Thorpe was born May 28, 1887. Running, jumping, and throwing better than almost anyone alive, he won Olympic gold medals in both the pentathlon and the decathlon in 1912.

🤰 Your Body at Twenty-Eight Weeks
Your womb now reaches well above your belly button, and you can feel it pressing on your ribs and stomach. Your body is carrying more blood, more fluid, and a fast-growing baby.
Third-trimester discomforts often show up now: back pain, heartburn, shortness of breath, swollen feet and ankles, leg cramps, trouble sleeping, needing to pass urine often, and Braxton Hicks tightenings. Most are normal. Rest, side sleeping, small meals, water, and gentle walks help.
Your doctor may check your iron again this trimester. Low iron is common in the third trimester, as your body makes more blood and your baby stores iron for the first months after birth. Keep eating iron foods with vitamin C.

🩺 Visits Every Two Weeks
From about Week 28, prenatal visits usually come every two weeks. From about Week 36, they usually come every week until birth.
At each visit, your doctor or midwife will check your blood pressure, your weight, the height of your womb, and your baby's heartbeat. They will ask about your baby's movements and any symptoms.
If your blood is Rh-negative, you will usually get the Rh shot around now. Many doctors also give the Tdap vaccine between Weeks 27 and 36. Bring your journal and your questions to every visit.

📝 Birth Preferences
Many mothers write a short list of birth preferences, sometimes called a birth plan. It is a way to think through what matters to you and to talk it over with your doctor or midwife before labor begins.
You might write who you want with you, how you hope to manage pain, whether you want to move around during labor, whether you want your baby placed skin to skin on your chest right after birth, and how you plan to feed your baby. You can even write that you would like the weekly song played or sung in the room.
Keep it short, one page or less. And hold it loosely. Labor does not always follow a plan, and sometimes your doctor will need to change course to keep you and your baby safe. That is not failure. That is God's GPS at work.

🎒 Starting Your Hospital Bag
You do not need to pack today, but start a list. Many mothers have their bag ready by about Week 36, and earlier is fine.
Common items: your ID and insurance card, a copy of your birth preferences, comfortable clothes and a robe, a nursing bra, toiletries, phone charger, snacks for Dad, an outfit and blanket for the baby to wear home, and the installed car seat. Add your headphones and the weekly songs, so the familiar music is with you in labor and in your baby's first hours.
Write the list in your journal and check items off as you gather them.

🩺 Following Up on the Placenta
At the anatomy scan, some mothers were told their placenta was lying low in the womb, near or over the cervix. In most cases, the placenta moves up and away as the womb grows. Your doctor will usually check again with an ultrasound in the third trimester, often around Week 32.
If the placenta is still covering the cervix, called placenta previa, your doctor will talk with you about a plan, which often includes a cesarean birth. You may be asked to avoid sex and heavy activity.
Call your doctor right away for any bleeding from the vagina in the third trimester, even if it is painless. Bleeding with a low placenta needs prompt care.

🧪 Third-Trimester Blood Tests
Around Week 28, your doctor may repeat some blood tests. A blood count checks for anemia, which is common in the third trimester as your blood volume grows. If your iron is low, your doctor may recommend an iron supplement.
If your blood is Rh-negative, an antibody screen is often done before the Rh shot. Some mothers are also retested for certain infections, depending on their health and where they live.
Ask what each test is for, and write the results in your journal. If you need iron, ask how to take it so your body absorbs it well and how to manage constipation it may cause.

🦶 A Myth About Movement
You may hear that babies move less near the end of pregnancy because they run out of room. This is a myth that can be dangerous.
It is true that movements may feel different, more like rolls and pushes than sharp kicks. But your baby should keep moving regularly right up to birth. A big drop in your baby's usual movement can be an early sign that something is wrong.
If your baby is moving much less than usual, call your doctor or midwife right away. Do not wait to see if it gets better tomorrow. Do not use a home heartbeat monitor to reassure yourself. Let your doctor check.

🧦 Swollen Legs and Support Socks
Mild swelling in the feet and ankles is common in the third trimester, especially at the end of the day and in hot weather. Your body holds more fluid, and the growing womb slows blood flow from the legs.
Put your feet up when you sit. Lie on your side. Avoid standing in one place for long. Walk or swim if your doctor agrees. Ask your doctor whether support or compression socks would help.
Call your doctor right away if swelling comes on suddenly, is in your face or hands, or comes with a headache or vision changes. Also call if one leg is much more swollen than the other, red, warm, or painful.

🙌 Saying Yes to Help
Many mothers find it hard to accept help. They feel they should be able to do everything. But the third trimester is a season to say yes.
When someone offers a meal, say yes. When someone offers to watch the older children, say yes. When someone offers to clean, run an errand, or drive you to an appointment, say yes and thank them.
The early church shared what they had so no one was in need. Accepting help is part of how God cares for families. One day, you will be the one bringing a meal to another new mother.

⚖️ Weight Gain in the Third Trimester
In the third trimester, many women gain about a pound a week, though this varies. Total healthy weight gain depends on your weight before pregnancy. For women who started at a healthy weight, doctors often suggest gaining about 25 to 35 pounds in all. Women who started with more weight are usually advised to gain less, and women who started underweight to gain more.
Much of the weight is not fat. It includes your baby, the placenta, the amniotic fluid, a larger womb, more blood, more fluid in your body, and breast growth.
Your doctor will check your weight at each visit. Focus on healthy food and gentle activity rather than the number on the scale. Tell your doctor about sudden weight gain, especially with swelling in your face or hands, since that can be a sign of high blood pressure.

🌧️ Feelings in the Final Trimester
The third trimester can bring big feelings. Excitement grows, and so can worry. You may feel impatient, emotional, or anxious about labor and caring for a newborn. Hormones and poor sleep make feelings stronger.
Talk with your husband and friends about how you feel. Write in your journal. Rest when you can. Keep singing, praying, and reading God's promises.
If you feel sad, hopeless, very anxious, or unable to enjoy life most days for two weeks or more, tell your doctor. Depression during pregnancy is common and treatable, and getting help now protects you and your baby.

🥗 Body: Caring for the Home This Week
In the third trimester, your baby is building iron stores and bones. Eat iron-rich foods such as beans, lentils, lean beef, chicken, and spinach, with a vitamin C food at the same meal. Keep up calcium foods like milk, yogurt, and pasteurized cheese. Eat smaller meals more often if heartburn or fullness bothers you.
Keep food safe through the end of pregnancy. Cook meat, eggs, chicken, and seafood completely. Wash produce. Choose pasteurized dairy. Heat deli meats until steaming. Pick low-mercury fish, and avoid shark, swordfish, king mackerel, and tilefish.
Alcohol is not known to be safe in any amount in pregnancy. Avoid smoking, vaping, and secondhand smoke. Keep caffeine under 200 mg a day. Ask before any medicine, herb, or supplement, and keep up gentle activity if your doctor says it is safe.

🚨 Signs to Call About Now
Call your doctor or midwife right away if your baby is moving much less than usual. Do not wait.
Also call right away for regular tightenings or cramps, a low backache that comes and goes, pressure in the pelvis, bleeding, fluid leaking or gushing, a severe headache, vision changes, sudden swelling of the face or hands, pain high on the right side of the belly, or a fever.
Know which hospital you will go to, how to get there, and who will drive you. Put it in your journal and on your phone.

👨 For Dad: The Home Stretch
Dad, welcome to the third trimester. This is when your support matters most. She is carrying more weight, sleeping less, and thinking about birth. Be close.
Learn how to help her notice the baby's movements. Sit with her during counting time, hand on her belly, and sing the weekly song together. When you feel a kick, count it.
Start practical preparations: the car seat, the safe sleep space, the route to the hospital. Sing action words with her: "hug," "kiss," "pray." Then do them.
Your voice on these phonic songs is the first kids music your child will ever know, so sing them often.

👵 For Grandparents and Siblings
Big brothers and sisters can act out the action words. Sing "jump" and jump. Sing "hug" and hug Mom. Sing "sleep" and pretend to snore. They will remember these songs and teach them to the baby.
Grandparents can help plan for after birth. Who will care for the older children during labor? Who will bring meals? Write the plan in the journal.
Children learn nursery rhymes and lullabies by singing them again and again, so let them sing the baby music with you every day.

🎶 One Song, Three Ways: Week 28
Every week has one GUP song, learned three different ways. A good preschool teacher never teaches an important lesson only once. Teach it three ways, and it is remembered.
Hear it. In the morning, listen once with your eyes closed. Thank God for bringing your baby into the third trimester.
Hum it. At midday, put on headphones and hum along. Then sing "sing, pray, hug, kiss" to the tune, doing each action as you sing.
Write it. In the evening, listen with your Pregnancy Journal open. Write the phonograms you hear, and build one action word from them for your Word List page.
GUP songs are baby music with a purpose: gentle like lullabies, repeating like nursery rhymes, and full of the phonic songs that become the building blocks of reading.

📓 Your Pregnancy Journal: Week-28 Pages
On your Word List page, add this week's action words with their phonograms and beats.
Start a "Daily Movement" page. Each day, write the time you counted, how many movements you felt, and how long it took. You will quickly learn your baby's normal.
On a "Third Trimester Plan" page, list your hospital, your route, your driver, and who will care for older children. Add a prayer for the final season.

🧭 God's GPS
The third trimester can bring surprises. A blood pressure reading may be high. A growth scan may be ordered. Your baby may be head-down or not. You may be told to rest more.
You make your plans, and God directs your steps. He has been directing them since the day this child was conceived, and He will direct them all the way to the birthday.
📖 “The heart of man disposes his way. But it is for the Lord to direct his steps.” (Proverbs 16:9, CPDV)
🎂 Jimmy Carter was born October 1, 1924. After serving as president of the United States, he taught Sunday school at his small Georgia church for decades and spent his later years building homes for families in need.

🙏 A Prayer for Week 28
"Father God, thank You for bringing us into the third trimester. You began this good work, and You will finish it. Thank You for blinking eyes, a growing brain, and every kick that tells us our baby is here.
Help us to notice, to listen, and to call for help when we need it. Fill our baby out with strength. Finish the lungs, the brain, and every part. Let our home be full of action words of love: sing, pray, hug, and kiss. Direct our steps all the way to the day we meet. In Jesus' name, amen."

❓ Questions Parents Ask
How do I count my baby's movements? Ask your doctor how they want you to do it. A common way is to count until you feel 10 movements while resting, usually in less than two hours. Know your baby's normal pattern.
What if my baby moves less than usual? Call your doctor or midwife right away. Do not wait until the next day, and do not rely on a home monitor.
How often will I see my doctor now? Usually every two weeks from about Week 28, and every week from about Week 36.
Why do I need the Rh shot? If your blood is Rh-negative and your baby's is Rh-positive, the shot keeps your body from making antibodies that could harm this or a future baby.
When do I call my doctor right away? Call for much less movement than usual, bleeding, leaking fluid, regular tightenings, pelvic pressure, a severe headache, vision changes, sudden swelling of the face or hands, or a fever.

✅ Your Week-28 Checklist
I took my prenatal vitamin every day. I noticed my baby's movements every day. I asked about the Rh shot and Tdap. I wrote my third trimester plan.
I heard, hummed, and wrote this week's one song every day. I sang action words and did the actions. I added them to my Word List. Dad sang and counted kicks with me. The family acted out the words.

📚 Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. To maintain medical accuracy, every lesson is fact-checked by Grok (Sal). General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.

I thanked the Minister for Georgia’s longstanding partnership with WHO and its valuable contribution to regional health cooperation, including through its expertise in tuberculosis control and efforts to eliminate hepatitis B and C.

We also discussed important priorities for Georgia, including improving medical education, addressing the migration of health professionals and making better use of AI and innovation to deliver safer, more affordable care.

If elected WHO Director-General, I will work to strengthen this networked approach, making WHO a platform that connects national expertise, shares successful solutions and helps countries achieve more together.

text:
The Trump administration is pressuring Lithuania to ease European sanctions against Belarus in order to facilitate the import of low-cost fertilizers into the United States.

Washington’s goal is to secure larger supplies of Belarusian potash—a key raw material for agricultural fertilizers—while simultaneously reducing American reliance on Canada, currently one of the primary suppliers of potash to the U.S.

However, the matter carries significant political implications: removing or relaxing European restrictions would allow the regime of Alexander Lukashenko to recover a substantial portion of its export revenue.

According to POLITICO, citing four European officials, the U.S. special envoy for Belarus, John Coale, has intensified contacts with Lithuanian diplomats in recent weeks to gauge Vilnius’s willingness to loosen trade restrictions.

The primary objective is reportedly to reopen the Lithuanian port of Klaipėda to the transit of Belarusian potash. Before the sanctions were imposed, approximately 90% of Belarus’s potash fertilizer exports passed through this port. Washington has also explored the possibility of utilizing other Baltic ports, including the port of Riga in Latvia.

The issue is particularly sensitive because the European sanctions against the Lukashenko regime were introduced following the 2020 presidential election—which the EU did not recognize as legitimate—and the subsequent violent crackdown on popular protests. These restrictions were later tightened following the Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, partly in light of the support Minsk provided for Russia’s aggression. European measures must be renewed unanimously every twelve months. The next renewal is scheduled for February 2027. Lithuania, which will assume the rotating presidency of the Council of the EU at the beginning of 2027, could theoretically block the renewal, causing the restrictions to lapse.

However, the American proposal faces strong opposition in Eastern Europe. Several European officials fear that a resumption of exports would allow Lukashenko to regain significant economic revenue, while simultaneously bolstering his international legitimacy and the regime's capacity to continue repressing and imprisoning political opponents.

An Eastern European official, quoted by POLITICO, described the American position in particularly harsh terms: the United States is reportedly applying diplomatic pressure, but the European response has been categorical: "No, absolutely not." The official added that if the Americans cannot learn from history, the Europeans must stand firm.

There is also a significant precedent: in March 2026, Washington had already eased certain U.S. sanctions against Belarus—including those targeting major companies in the fertilizer sector—as part of a diplomatic agreement with Minsk that led to the release of 250 political prisoners.

Furthermore, in September, Trump publicly announced that he was working on a major trade deal to purchase Belarusian potash at prices lower than those offered by Canadian suppliers. The following day, however, Lukashenko stated that Belarus had no surplus fertilizer available for supply to the United States.

The political crux is clear: Washington is seeking economic benefits for American farmers, while Europe fears that the price of such a deal would be a further weakening of sanctions against a regime allied with Moscow. The issue concerns not only the trade in fertilizers, but also the consistency of Western policy toward the authoritarian regimes that support Russia’s aggression against Ukraine.

text:
I would agree but would put it like this: the chances of Iran making a deal are much more than zero, but principally and only for a deal that is unlikely on offer, being one that is very close to Iran’s stated terms and sequencing. 

Conversely, having endured this long, the probability of Iran spending its leverage now on what it regards as a bad deal is, I think, much closer to zero. 

Iran certainly will not want (and the current regime actors would unlikely survive) making a deal that is weaker than the MoU, or repeats its errors, which from their perspective related to sequencing. 

The trouble is Trump now regards even the MoU as a mistake and a waste of time. Flowing from that, Washington accepting Iran’s new, current preferred conditions and sequencing would be very surprising. Making a deal that is even more favourable to Iran than the MoU would be portrayed as a significant US climbdown. Upfront release of assists, removal of sanctions and lifting the blockade likely in return for opacity on “agreeing to agree” something on nuclear, and Hormuz terms that are deeply problematic is not a “win” for the US. And let’s be clear (as this gets sketched over in coverage): the Hormuz “reopening”, the prize Iran offers at the end of its preferred sequencing, isn’t a return to the status quo ante. If you read Iran’s interpretation in the widely covered Iran-Oman transit arrangements, it is legitimisation of their ability to control traffic without needing to bomb. All this would be very hard for the US to sell as a win. 

But the more important question is whether this really is peak Iranian leverage? I’m not convinced it is. Roll forward a fortnight. Suppose renewed US strikes are followed by Iranian retaliation, Hormuz remains contested and regional infrastructure is being hit. Whether you agree with them or not, Iran would argue they had just cause to retaliate and this would provide context for the public backing from the usual suspects on the international stage (Russia, China etc). The economic and market consequences would be severe. And just because Trump would no longer face an immediate ballot-box consequence  (the midterms would be over) it doesn’t mean he could evade the political and geopolitical pressure created by the significant further deterioration in global markets, and the global economy, that would result. Yes, Iran would likely suffer significant damage to their own infrastructure but they weathered thousands of strikes on epic fury, and the regime still maintained capacity to rule, and to fight. Would Iran’s leverage then be greater or smaller than it is today? 

Or let’s take an alternative path, one that also seems to be on the table. The US maintains the blockade and sanctions pressure, but oil prices remain elevated and the economic damage accumulates as we head into 2027. OECD countries sink into recession. Sure, Iran is also under pressure in this scenario but the regime carries on regardless. Again, is Iran’s leverage necessarily lower than today, or is it higher? 

That is why I think Iran sees the current period as a window in which it should test what its leverage will buy, not necessarily one in which it must spend that leverage if the answer is “not enough”. I also think Iran knows that leverage can decay, but it can also compound, and that its own actions - more than the midterms - will determine its future leverage.

It is entirely possible I am wrong. Maybe a miraculous deal will be made. I hope so. I just don’t see it.
